title: Support for the summary of the contributions to the exploratory consultation on the future of the communications sector and its infrastructure
description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 
The tender relates to the launch by the European Commission on 23 February 2023 of an exploratory consultation on the future of the electronic communications sector and its infrastructure to gather views on the potential developments of the connectivity sector and its infrastructure (“Exploratory Consultation”). The Exploratory Consultation will close on 19 May 2023. 
The Exploratory Consultation, which includes a questionnaire of 62 questions, investigates technological and market developments including their impact on future networks and business models for electronic communications; consumers related aspects, barriers to Single Market and fair contribution by all players benefitting from the digital transformation. 
The contractor would be requested to review and summarise all the contributions of the respondents to the Exploratory Consultation to which it will be given access, and to produce the following summary reports:
1.	Preliminary Summary Report
The Preliminary Summary Report will consist of a summary of the contributions to the Exploratory Consultation relating only to questions 1, 2, 6, 7, 11 and 33. The Preliminary Summary Report shall be limited to six (6) pages maximum. 
2.	Summary Report
The Summary Report will consist of a summary overview of all the replies received by the Commission to the Exploratory Consultation. The Summary Report should present the information obtained during the Exploratory Consultation in a descriptive format. The Summary Report shall be limited to 15 pages maximum. 
3.	In-Depth Summary Report
The In-depth Summary Report will consist of a comprehensive summary of all the contributions to the Exploratory Consultation, question by question, distinguishing between categories of respondents. The In-depth Summary Report shall be limited to 65 to 80 pages maximum.
The three summary reports must be produced in sequence and delivered on specific dates, and in any event, within maximum 7 weeks, after the date of closure of the Exploratory Consultation on 19 May 2023. 
The potential contractor should be able to allocate sufficient time and resources to the production of the summary reports within the deadlines, taking into account that it is not possible at this stage to provide an estimate of the number of contributions to be reviewed and summarised. 
Estimated total maximum: € 60,000
Maximum contract duration: 6 months

contractingAuthority: null
ragText:
Procurement: Study and Technical Assistance for the Extension of the Support for Broadband rollout Pages (SFBR) of the Shaping Europe’s digital future Website
Call identifier: CNECT/2023/MVP/0081-ExA
Contracting authority: null
Description: Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 
Study and Technical Assistance for the Extension of the Support for Broadband rollout Pages (SFBR) of the Shaping Europe’s digital future Website including an update of the study on National Broadband Plans and of the applications for the annual Broadband Award.

The main objectives of this study are:
- to complete and improve the content of the existing version of the support for broadband rollout pages (SFBR) of the shaping europe’s digital future website by analysing new studies and other sources of current information on broadband technologies, economies and policies;
- to regularly update the whole content of the SFBR including the 27 country overview pages every six months and in this context;
- to develop an update of the “study on national broadband plans (NBP’S) in the eu-27” including the analyse of the NBP’S adjustment of each MS to the gigabit and 5g targets of 2025 and 2030; 
- to especially run of the site and to promote all activities of CEF Digital; 
- to carry out and evaluate the European broadband award in 2024 and 2025 and
- to cooperate with the support facility office of the BCO network concerning the communication by the SFBR pages and the Broadband Europe newsletter.

title: Smart Industrial Remoting: Remote Working in Non-digitalised Industries - Pilot Project - CNECT/2021/OP/0011
description: Smart Industrial Remoting is a pilot project addressing the digitalisation needs of selected industrial ecosystems strategic to the EU economy. It will use the network of Digital Innovation Hubs to promote the findings, and the developed tool box, to the SMEs in those regions within the chosen industrial sectors.The objectives are to:• map existing digital tools enabling digitalisation/remote working within (at least three) critical EU industrial ecosystems and perform a gap analysis for each. The work shall focus on SMEs from regions with a low digital intensity;• identify the needs and requirements for a toolbox for digitalisation/remote working within the chosen ecosystems;• involve a wide number of stakeholders, including Digital Innovation Hubs, to develop and promote existing and newly developed digital tools targeting those industries. The project shall outline concrete policy and industry actions.

title: European Parliament Pilot Project — European Green Digital Coalition — CNECT/2021/OP/0005
description: Currently there is no standardised method for assessing the positive impact of digitalisation on the environment and climate. It is not clear what is the net environmental impact of digitalisation in a given sector or in a specific scenario. This leads to lack of clarity for private and public investors which digitalisation projects are eligible for sustainable financing. This EP Pilot project will support the recently established European Green Digital Coalition (EGDC) to deliver on its commitments. It will support the secretariat and functioning of the EGDC, analyse many digital solutions applied to a given scenarios and develop a methodology for assessment of net environmental impact. The guidance documents on green digital transformation will be developed for different sectors and for the ICT sector in cooperation with relevant sectoral stakeholders. A consultation and dissemination workshop will be organised across EU, as well as a high level event, by the end of 2022.

title: EU Blockchain Pre-commercial Procurement
description: This pre-commercial procurement (PCP) supports the development of new capabilities for the future version of the European Blockchain Service Infrastructure (EBSI) to enable the implementation of various use cases with high volume and velocity requirements whist enhancing the sustainability, security, interoperability and robustness aspects. The aim is to go beyond what existing blockchain solutions can offer. This PCP is done in relation to the work of the European Blockchain Partnership, a cooperation between the European Commission, all EU Member States and some countries of the European Economic Area to deliver together the EBSI. PCP progressively selects the best value for money solutions that the market can develop by awarding R&D service contracts to a number of providers in parallel in a phased approach that covers solution design, prototyping, solution development, installation and testing. PCP thus provides a first customer reference for contractors with innovative solutions.

title: Bespoke Service to Support the Cyber Situation and Analysis Centre for the European Commission
description: In the wake of Russia’s military aggression, the EU ‘is considering further steps to prevent, discourage, deter and respond to malicious behaviour in cyberspace’. To support these objectives a cybersecurity situational awareness and analysis centre would assist the Commission in supporting situational awareness and coordinated response to crises, including those of a hybrid nature, in line with the Commission’s existing competences and responsibilities.The overall objective of the contract is to provide a bespoke service to support the scoping, design and development of an EU cybersecurity situational awareness and analysis centre for the Commission.The three specific objectives for the contract are set out below:1. set up a virtual situation centre;2. review best practice and support the setting up of a physical situation centre;3. ensure full interoperability with EU entities responsible for cybersecurity situational awareness and analysis.

title: Pilot Project: EU Innovation Procurement Observatory – CNECT/2022/OP/0055
description: This procurement aims set up an observatory that tracks national policy frameworks/initiatives and investments on innovation procurement in the digital economy around Europe and that engages public buyers, policy makers and citizens across Europe to share good practices. Using public investments smartly to speed up the adoption of innovative solutions is crucial for successful digital, green economic recovery. Europe needs to step up its game to safeguard its global competitiveness. Objective is to raise political visibility and impetus across countries around Europe to make this happen. Greater political engagement with continued regular EU wide monitoring can reinforce the impact of economic recovery plans. It can encourage countries to set higher ambitions for modernising public services with more cutting-edge solutions, which creates simultaneously high value jobs, including for innovative startups and SMEs.

title: Funding Gaps on the Path to the Digital Decade
description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle value procedure (read more here). 

DG CNECT requests the procurement of a Study aimed at estimating investment gaps to reach the 2030 Digital Decade targets. The Study should specifically focus on the analysis of private investment expected in each area of the 2030 Digital Compass and that are in the scope of the Digital Europe Programme, thus complementing an ongoing DG CNECT Study that focuses on public investment expectations.

The present Study should provide evidence of the monetary gaps to achieve the 2030 Digital Decade targets at both the EU and national level and make recommendations as regards the possibilities to cover these, particularly focusing on those areas that could be supported by the Work Programme 2025-2027 of the Digital Europe Programme and by potential future financial products under InvestEU.

In addition, this Study should provide two sets of recommendations. Having in mind the areas for Multi-Country Projects proposed in the Annex to the Digital Decade Policy Programme, it should identify areas for further development of such large-scale projects. Finally, the Study should provide recommendations related to forms of Commission’s funding and alternative forms of funding which may bring sufficient leveraging effect to bridge the monetary gaps.

The results of this Study should be consolidated in a final comprehensive report, representing the main deliverable of the Contract

title: Study on Mobile Satellite Services (MSS) in the 2 GHz Band in the EU – Implementation of the Current Regulatory Framework and an Overview of the Satellite Connectivity Market
description: The study has the following specific objectives:1. to provide an objective qualitative and quantitative assessment of the implementation of the Union’s current 2 GHz MSS framework, to give an overview of the 2 GHz MSS spectrum usage and services offered. The analysis should pay special attention to any divergences that may have arisen in implementation at national level;2. to outline current state of play as well as developments and trends in the broader satellite connectivity market globally (e.g. new entrants, services, orbits, mergers), the competitive landscape, the drivers at EU level and globally and the role of the EU players;3. to outline possible usage scenarios for the 2 GHz spectrum after 2027, in line with relevant EU policies and programmes, including the Digital Decade targets and upcoming Secure Connectivity programme.

title: Fostering Digitisation of Public Sector and Green Transition in Europe through the Use of an Innovative European GovTech Platform - CNECT/LUX/2021/OP/0053
description: This pilot project aims to support public administrations in the adoption of cost-effective and flexible digital solutions by introducing the GovTech ecosystem to the European public sector. By following and scaling up the GovTech platform model, already used in different forms by GovTech Labs around Europe, public administrations across Europe can work together more easily to solve shared challenges and more cost-effectively to adapt existing projects to their individual needs. The use of the GovTech model across the EU will offer benefits of scale to both public administrations and providers of digital services. Such providers, in particular innovative European SMEs and start-ups, will gain recognition as trusted partners in the delivery of modern digital solutions for public services. The overall aim is to boost the European GovTech market and help public administrations access tailor-made digital solutions, thus fostering modernisation of Europe’s public sector.

description: Sourcing of data and evidence for policy design and implementation of Trans European Digital Networks (TEN-D) complementing the Cable Projects of European Interest (CPEI) exercise. This study should analyse potential gaps in capacity, resilience and security of terrestrial links, taking into account the expected developments in the field of data centres and other AI facilities as proposed in the Cloud and AI Development Act (CADA). title: Evaluation report of the ECCC required under Article 38(4) of Regulation (EU) 2021/887
description:
The contractor will support the European Commission, under Article 38(4) of Regulation (EU) 2021/887, in carrying out a comprehensive evaluation of the European Cybersecurity Competence Centre following the submission of its implementation report. The evaluation will assess the effectiveness of the ECCC’s mandate, its legal and administrative framework, and the functioning of its governance and coordination mechanisms, taking into account input from the Governing Board, National Coordination Centres and the wider cybersecurity community.

The study will also examine the extent to which the ECCC creates synergies with other Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies, and identify opportunities to reduce fragmentation, overlaps and inefficiencies within the EU cybersecurity ecosystem.

Procurement: Technological developments and roaming study
Call identifier: EC-CNECT/2026/MVP/0166-EXA
Contracting authority: European Commission, DG CNECT - Communications Networks, Content and Technology
Description: The purpose of this study is to assess the availability of technologies, services and business models which could potentially act as alternatives to regulated retail voice, SMS and data roaming services.
It will examine the competitive pressure that existing and emerging alternatives, technological developments and traffic flows may exert on roaming services. 

The study will support the EC’s analysis of the functioning of the roaming market, including the provision of roaming services at retail and wholesale level. The assessments and conclusions will feed into the EC’s 2027 review of the roaming market and inform the report to be submitted to the European Parliament and Council in accordance with the Roaming Regulation. 

The technologies and services covered by the study shall include mobile networks and other electronic communication network, such as fixed and satellite networks. 
The study shall analyse the impact of these services (referred to as “Alternative Services”) on roaming in the EU/EEA and the way it is regulated. 
The study should consider, inter alia, the following developments: 
• eSIM and iSIM technologies; 
• 5G Stand Alone, 5G Advanced and Early 6G Developments;
• Satellite communication services; 
• Mobile virtual network operators;
• Network evolution; 
• Wi-Fi offloading/ Wi-Fi aggregation; and 
• OTTs and messaging evolution.

Maximum value of the procurement: 139.999 EUR - Contract duration 5 months.

title: Quality of Service performance of roaming services study
description:
The purpose of this study is to assess the quality-of-service (QoS) performance of mobile network operators under the Roaming Regulation. The study will assess if roaming customers receive the same QoS when roaming as they usually have at home. It will measure the performance of roaming and domestic mobile services against the following minimum QoS parameters: 
(1) data download speed; 
(2) data upload speed; 
(3) latency; and 
(4) available network technology and generation. 

The dataset on roaming subscribers will be compared with the corresponding datasets for:
(i)	the same subscribers in their home network; 
(ii)	domestic subscribers on the visited network; and 
(iii)	other roaming subscribers on the same visited network. 

The findings will support the EC’s analysis of the functioning of the roaming market, including the provision of roaming services at retail and wholesale level as well as the effectiveness of the QoS obligations. The data, analysis and conclusions of the study will feed into the EC’s 2027 review of the roaming market and inform the report to be submitted to the European Parliament and Council in accordance with the Roaming Regulation.

Maximum value of the procurement: 100.000 EUR - Contract duration 5 months.

title: Study 2026-006 – Supporting the Commission Expert Group on the Security and Resilience of Submarine Cable Infrastructures
description:
The purpose of the study will be to support the Submarine Cable Infrastructure informal Expert Group in the course of 2026/2027, notably by assessing regularly and providing recommendations aiming at improving the security and resilience of existing and new submarine cable infrastructures, and by supporting the deployment or significant upgrade of submarine cable infrastructures via Cable Projects of European Interest (‘CPEIs’). It is a direct follow-up of the Commission Recommendation (EU) 2024/779 on Secure and Resilient Submarine Cable Infrastructures and the implementation of the 2025 EU Action Plan on Cable Security. 

The reason for purchasing is the high level of specialisation required, especially as regards the economic and technological aspects of submarine cable infrastructures, as well as the necessity to swiftly deliver on this important topic relying on limited internal resources.

title: Analysis of users' engagement with Generative AI features within Search Engines
description:
This study aims to provide methodologically rigorous, empirical data on user
engagement with generative AI features integrated into online search engines. The
contractor will be expected to measure, through observational and experimental
methods, how these features affect user behaviour, query reformulation, session
duration, and time spent on AI-generated content relative to organic results. The study will further characterise users' visual attention and information intake using eye-tracking or equivalent attention-measurement techniques, covering AI-generated answers, their citations, and surrounding organic results, and evaluate users' trust in AI- generated content, their verification behaviour, and their ability to recognise such content. These effects will be examined across different Member States, languages and demographics - with particular attention to vulnerable groups - and across query categories of public interest. (Maximum value of the procurement : 139,999 EUR Contract duration 12 months)

title: Analysis of the Online Pornography Ecosystem from a European Perspective
description: The study pursues two main, closely interconnected aims: enhancing transparency and clarifying platform ownership within the online pornography ecosystem. By combining these two dimensions, the study enables a more comprehensive understanding of both how platforms present themselves externally and how they are structured internally, and will provide a comprehensive, evidence-based analysis of the European online pornography ecosystem, examining its structure, business models, and interdependencies across the digital value chain. The research will generate a holistic understanding of how the sector operates economically, legally, and technologically within Europe, including its intersections with other mainstream platforms and the wider digital economy. title: Women in Digital (WiD) Platform – EU Coordination
description:
The EU faces severe challenges in attracting girls and women into the information and communications technology (ICT) sector. Less than one in five ICT specialists employed in the Union are female. This initiative addresses the Digital Decade target of improving gender balance while reaching 20 million ICT specialists by 2030, by supporting activities that actively tackle the under-representation of girls and women in the ICT sector in the EU.

This action will build on and further develop the work initiated by the WIDCON project (101195389), funded under the DIGITAL work programme 2023-2024. It will support community building and cross-fertilisation across the EU, by creating an online EU platform (as a sub-domain of the Digital Skills and Jobs Platform) for Women in Digital resources that will scale up the exchange of good practices, data gathering, policy mapping, and outreach and awareness raising activities across the MS. Moreover, it will coordinate and expand the network and community of experts set up by the WIDCON project and create and coordinate a network of relevant contacts in each Member State, to expand and strengthen the EU Women in Digital network.

description:
This is the renewal of the first Simpl PSO Framework contract, which was awarded in 2023 following the publication of calls for tenders CNECT/2023/OP/0050: https://etendering.ted.europa.eu/cft/cft-display.html?cftId=14888 .
The objective of PSOII call for tenders is to procure services to support and improve Simpl programme quality management system built to ensure a high and stable quality level of the IT products related to Simpl programme. 
It is also meant to strengthen the project management support and horizontal coordination tasks across the involved stakeholders, boosting efficient processes inspired by open-source best practices while complying to European Commission procurement rules. 
The PSO II framework contract will follow up on the existing PSO framework contract after it ends of delivery of the third specific contract (September 2026).

title: AI for Public Good Lot 1 (Health: Innovative AI-based cancer imaging solutions for breast and prostate diagnosis) and Lot 2 (Energy: Innovative AI-based solutions for electric grid optimization)
description:
The European Commission is committed to tapping into the potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to collaboratively and complementarily drive research to address global challenges. 
DG CONNECT is the European Commission’s Directorate General responsible for digital policies. Through its Directorate A “Artificial Intelligence Office”, it is tasked to implement the AI Act and promote the development and use of trustworthy AI. Additionally, it focuses on creating solutions for societal good, while also facilitating the implementation of international AI agreements to contribute to a global approach to AI. 
The purpose of this call for tenders is to develop and test AI-powered solutions for the benefit of the EU as well as wider communities and third countries. The call has two lots, on AI for Cancer imaging (LOT1) and on AI for Electric grid optimisation (LOT2).
LOT 1 will explore and demonstrate how AI-powered solutions applied to EU cancer imaging data can be further fine-tuned and applied in other locations and settings covering a large variety of populations, without transferring the underlying sensitive health data. It has two predefined use-cases, breast cancer and prostate cancer.
LOT2 will support the European Commission in exploring and demonstrating the application of AI- powered solutions to effectively tackle challenges within energy systems, specifically focusing on the seamless integration of renewable energy sources (RES) capacity across diverse energy system levels.

Procurement: AI for Public Good Lot 1 (Health: Innovative AI-based cancer imaging solutions for breast and prostate diagnosis) and Lot 2 (Energy: Innovative AI-based solutions for electric grid optimization)
Call identifier: EC-CNECT/2026/OP/0003
Contracting authority: European Commission, DG CNECT - Communications Networks, Content and Technology
Description: The European Commission is committed to tapping into the potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to collaboratively and complementarily drive research to address global challenges. 
DG CONNECT is the European Commission’s Directorate General responsible for digital policies. Through its Directorate A “Artificial Intelligence Office”, it is tasked to implement the AI Act and promote the development and use of trustworthy AI. Additionally, it focuses on creating solutions for societal good, while also facilitating the implementation of international AI agreements to contribute to a global approach to AI. 
The purpose of this call for tenders is to develop and test AI-powered solutions for the benefit of the EU as well as wider communities and third countries. The call has two lots, on AI for Cancer imaging (LOT1) and on AI for Electric grid optimisation (LOT2).
LOT 1 will explore and demonstrate how AI-powered solutions applied to EU cancer imaging data can be further fine-tuned and applied in other locations and settings covering a large variety of populations, without transferring the underlying sensitive health data. It has two predefined use-cases, breast cancer and prostate cancer.
LOT2 will support the European Commission in exploring and demonstrating the application of AI- powered solutions to effectively tackle challenges within energy systems, specifically focusing on the seamless integration of renewable energy sources (RES) capacity across diverse energy system levels.

title: Monitoring of the development and implementation of ICT standards and standardisation deliverables in ITU-T
description:
External Consultants as ICT Standardisation Experts for DG CNECT in targeted standardisation groups across ITU-T and other relevant technical bodies in ISO & IEC
Background and objectives:
The International affairs and Policy outreach Unit (DG CNECT.DDG2.1) is the Unit in DG CONNECT in charge of international issues, including the coordination of matters related to information and communication technologies (ICT) standardisation, and representing the EU in the International Telecommunication Union standardisation sector (ITU-T).

The objective of the EU regarding international standardisation, as stated in the Communication setting an EU Strategy on Standardisation[1], aims at reinforcing EU’s leading position as forerunner in key technologies and promoting core EU values in global standardisation. 
The International Digital Strategy[2] of the European Union also calls for shaping a global digital governance and standards with a network of partners, promoting its values-based approach on digital standards to shape a global digital transformation that is human-centric, trustworthy, and respects human rights and fundamental freedoms, acting decisively to become a driving force of responsibly guided technological advancement on the global stage.
The EU acknowledges the important role of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) in the context of global standardisation and believes that the EU and its Member States must promote a more strategic approach to international standardisation activities, namely in the ITU.
The purpose of this tender is to contract the services of standardisation experts to follow closely the ITU-T standardisation work in key sensitive topics defined by CNECT.DDG2.1 Unit, and report regularly to CNECT.DDG2.1 on relevant findings and trends with respect to EU digital policies, and proactively suggest potential strategic actions for DG CNECT to consider, in particular the need of more involvement of EU experts in technical bodies, study groups and working groups of ITU-T.
The consultants will act as observers on behalf of DG CNECT in targeted standardisation groups across ITU-T. They will follow closely ITU-T standardisation work in key sensitive topics defined by DG CNECT.DDG2.1. Maximum total value of the contract:135.000 EUR.

title: Implementation report of the ECCC required under Article 38(2) of Regulation (EU) 2021/887
description:
Regulation (EU) 2021/887 of the European Parliament and of the Council established the European Cybersecurity Industrial, Technology and Research Competence Centre (ECCC) and the Network of National Coordination Centres (NCCs) to strengthen the Union’s leadership and strategic autonomy in cybersecurity (hereinafter “the Regulation”). The Regulation entrusts the ECCC with the coordination of Union cybersecurity research, innovation, and industrial activities, notably under the Digital Europe Programme (DEP) and Horizon Europe. 
Pursuant to Article 38(2) of the Regulation, the European Commission shall prepare an implementation report, which will be submitted to the European Parliament and to the Council The implementation report shall take into account the preliminary input of the Governing Board, the national coordination centres and the Community. 
The Competence Centre and Member States shall provide the Commission with the information necessary for the preparation of that report. On the basis of the conclusions of the implementation report, the Commission may take appropriate actions.
The contract concerns the provision of external expertise, information and data gathering and analytical support for the drafting of the above-mentioned implementation report. The contractor shall support with gathering of information and evidence, related assessment and drafting of the implementation report. The overall objective of the resulting contract would be to support the Commission in preparing the Article 38(2) implementation report and assessment of the ECCC by delivering robust, traceable evidence and analytical inputs. Maximum total contract value: 139,500 EUR.

title: Study on the expected investment return of commercial digital submarine cables to establish a profitability benchmark for CEF Digital
description:
Subject of procurement is the development of a financial benchmark to assess the commercial viability of digital submarine cables. The study will serve as an input for the evaluation of funding applications under the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) Digital programme, specifically under the future Digital Global Gateways call for proposals. It will gather data about past commercial projects and collect opinions from market players. After clean up and triangulation of the data collected to ensure comparability, the study will calculate the historical average investment return of cable system projects and run statistical analysis to identify key profitability drivers.
The study is expected to determine an expected/benchmark return on investment that would be used to compare the profitability of the projects being evaluated and assess how much they rely on public funds to be rolled out.
Maximum total value of the contract: 50 000 EUR and Maximum Duration: 4 months

title: A framework for the systematic comparison between the DSA Transparency reports & the DSA Transparency Database submissions
description:
The objective of the support contract is to develop a systematic framework to compare and benchmark the data generated through the two main content moderation transparency data sources of the DSA: the transparency reports and the DSA Transparency Database. 

To test and apply this framework, the support contract will develop a methodology to compare the data reported in one cycle of VLOPs and VLOSEs’ transparency reports with their statements of reasons submissions to the DSA Transparency Database in the same timeframe to check for (in)consistencies in the reporting. In performing this comparison, the support contract should take into account (differences in) the relevant legal bases of the two data sources and document the comparative methodology developed for future use. The comparison should be made using the reports that will be published according to the Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2835 of 4 November 2024 and the updated Transparency Database schema.

The focus of the support contract should be on developing meaningful, per-platform quantitative indicators reports published in the covered timeframe., The support contract should also propose operational recommendations for compliance monitoring, including recommendations for future schema updates to the DSA Transparency Database or improvements to the Transparency Reports’' templates. 

The insights gained from this support contract will support the Commission in its supervision and enforcement work.

title: User observations on usage of recommender systems to enable scaling of recommender systems experiments through automated and agentic means
description:
Pursuant to article 27 DSA, providers of online platforms must clearly explain in their terms and conditions the main parameters used in their recommender systems, using plain and intelligible language. Moreover, they must explain options for users to modify or influence these main parameters. The main parameters that must be explained include (a) the most significant criteria used to determine suggested information, and (b) the reasons for the relative importance of these parameters. For platforms offering multiple options for recommender systems, they must provide a functionality allowing users to select and modify their preferred option at any time. Such a functionality should be directly and easily accessible from the section of the platform’s interface where the information is prioritized. In addition to the obligations established by article 27, providers of VLOPs and VLOSEs have an additional requirement: they must provide at least one recommender system option that is not based on profiling as defined in Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (“General Data Protection Regulation” or “GDPR”). 

These transparency requirements aim to give users more control and understanding of how information is presented to them on online platforms, particularly in relation to personalized recommendations. 

Against this background, this contract will explore how users engage with recommender systems across Very Large Online Platforms (VLOPs) and Very Large Online Search Engine (VLOSEs) through user surveys and user observations. 

DG CONNECT, together with the European Centre for Algorithmic Transparency at the Joint Research Centre (ECAT – JRC), is developing new methods to analyze recommender systems. These methods are developed across a wide range of representative recommendation surfaces across VLOPs and VLOSEs (both in terms of user experience – social media feeds, products listing, etc. - and types of contents – video, text, images, products, etc.). Therefore, the need arises to ground the understanding of such systems with real world data from observations of user interactions with recommender systems, confronting state of the art of the scientific literature with the reality of a representative panel of VLOPs and VLOSEs’ user base (in terms of relevant demographic variables such as age, gender, computer literacy, etc.).

title: Feasibility Study on Unified and interoperable system that will reinforce synergies in the context of eCommerce
description:
The European Commission, and in particular the General Directorates involved in marketplace and custom activities such as the DG CONNECT, DG GROW and DG JUST, is seeking proposals for a feasibility study aimed at integrating and optimizing existing databases to enhance the detection and tracking of non-compliant products found on online marketplaces throughout the EU.

The European Union currently operates several databases that collect and disseminate information on non-compliant products across different regulatory and institutional contexts. 

These systems serve distinct but partially overlapping purposes, and there is increasing interest in assessing whether more integrated or interoperable solutions could improve enforcement, transparency, and policy evaluation at EU level.

This study will assess the feasibility of merging or linking these systems more closely, to reduce fragmentation, improve data accessibility, and enhance cooperation between market surveillance and customs authorities. Duration 6 months Maximum Amount :142,000 EUR.

title: Longitudinal support contract on specific risks and harms that minors face in the EU digital environment over time
description:
Amidst the upcoming adoption of Commission’s Guidelines on article 28(1) of the DSA as well as other measures on the protection of minors in Q3 2025, there is a need to increase our understanding of how the risks, harms and benefits that children experience on online platforms evolve (also in light of a potential review of the Guidelines in 2027). In addition, it is important to supplement currently fragmented understanding about children’s perceptions of their online experiences, or knowledge about what children would want from tech companies to improve their safety, security and well-being online. Complementing the EU-wide inquiry into the impact of social media on well-being, this support contract would help monitoring children’s perspective on how EU rules are improving the digital environment over time.

The support contract aims at providing comprehensive and representative data on children’s online experiences in the EU over time, which would be accompanied by a monitoring measurement framework. This primary research would allow to monitor trends with regards to the risks, harms and benefits that children face online across the EU, as well as their perception of different platforms and characteristics thereof, and how they navigate those risks and opportunities of their digital environment. In particular, the support contract should aim at linking specific risks, harms, benefits, perceptions and behaviors to specific platforms, features, and/or uses thereof, to assess the impact of EU action on platforms via the DSA.

title: Digital Twin for Reconstruction: Innovative AI-powered solutions for urban reconstruction
description:
Digital Twin for Reconstruction: Innovative AI-powered solutions for urban reconstruction

DG CONNECT is the European Commission’s Directorate General responsible for digital policies. Through its Directorate A “Artificial Intelligence Office”, it is tasked to implementing the AI Act and promoting the development and use of trustworthy AI. Additionally, it focuses on creating solutions for societal good, while also facilitating the implementation of international AI agreements to contribute to a global approach to AI

The purpose of this call is to cover the AI office activities to develop and test AI-based solutions for the benefit of wider communities and third countries, initially focusing on Ukraine.

title: Study to assess the interaction between the DSA and the Member States' National Measures
description:
On 17 February 2024, Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (hereinafter, the “Digital Services Act” or the “DSA”), setting out a fully harmonized horizontal framework for the regulation of the activities of providers of intermediary services, entered into full application. 

As laid down in Article 1 of the DSA, the Regulation aims to contribute to the proper functioning of the internal market for intermediary services by establishing fully harmonized rules for a safe, predictable and reliable online environment. The DSA sets out a maximum harmonization EU regulatory framework for providers of intermediary services in the Union, laying down harmonized provisions.

The general objective of this study is to support the European Commission in its role of enforcer of the Treaties, which in this case requires assessing whether Member States have adapted their national legislation upon the DSA becoming fully applicable and identifying any remaining issues of overlap or possible incompatibility with the DSA. More specifically, the objective of the study is to produce a mapping of the existing and upcoming national measures applicable to providers of online intermediary services falling within the harmonized regulatory fields of the DSA. 

The study would provide a complete mapping of the existing or planned national legally binding acts (hereinafter, the ‘national measures’) in the subject matter covered by the DSA. These national measures are to be analyzed systematically with a view to identify any case where they might overlap and/or conflict with the DSA, thus also creating a risk of fragmentation of the Single Market.

Maximum total value of the contract: 50 000 EUR.
contractingAuthority: European Commission, DG CNECT - Communications Networks, Content and Technology

title: Study to assess Out-of-Court Dispute Settlement (ODS) bodies under Article 21 of the Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (Digital Services Act)
description:
The Digital Services Act (DSA) introduces certified out-of-court dispute settlement (ODS) bodies under Article 21 to enhance user redress mechanisms beyond internal complaint systems and judicial proceedings. These bodies offer users a neutral and independent forum for resolving disputes related to content moderation decisions by online platforms. Recognising the novelty and complexity of this mechanism, this study is dedicated to supporting the implementation of Article 21 by analysing cooperation between certified ODS bodies and online platforms. It will address both practical and legal challenges, including the assessment of case admissibility, information exchange, technical constraints, and financial considerations. By examining current practices and gathering feedback from stakeholders, the study aims to develop actionable recommendations to improve the ODS process.

The study’s findings will support the European Commission, the Digital Services Coordinators, and the European Board for Digital Services in their supervision and enforcement roles. Special attention will be given to challenges faced during the post-certification phase, drawing from experiences across Member States and a range of platform types and ODS bodies. The study will not only focus on legal obligations and procedural fairness but also on technical interoperability and case management models. Ultimately, it aims to foster more transparent and effective cooperation between platforms and ODS bodies, promote fairer content moderation, and reinforce user trust in digital services.
Maximum value of the procurement: 60.000 EUR - Contract duration 6 months

title: Gender-based violence and illegal content on pornographic platforms
description:
In December 2023, the European Commission designated three major pornography websites, Pornhub.com, Stripchat.com, and Xvideos.com, as Very Large Online Platforms (VLOPs). A fourth, XNXX.com, received the same designation in July 2024. In May 2025, the European Commission terminated the designation of Stripchat as a VLOP following an assessment, which concluded that Stripchat's number of average monthly active recipients in the EU had been lower than the relevant threshold for an uninterrupted period of one year. This call for tenders concentrates on Pornhub, XVideos, and XNXX, which will collectively be referred to as the “Three Designated Entities”.

The objective of the project is to generate evidence-based insights grounded in the lived experiences of performers, content creators, and victims who have been harmed by illegal content distributed through these services. The study will assess compliance with two major areas of the DSA.

First, it will examine the notice and action mechanisms established under Article 16, evaluating whether they are user-friendly, effective, and capable of processing reports in a timely, objective, and fair manner. This includes a particular focus on how platforms handle reports concerning child sexual abuse material, non-consensual intimate image sharing, cyberstalking, and unauthorized use of copyrighted material, while also considering the potential for misuse of these systems by bad-faith actors.

Second, the study will focus on risk assessment and mitigation measures required under Articles 34 and 35, analyzing how these platforms verify the identity, age, and consent of individuals appearing in uploaded or livestreamed content. This analysis will also explore how performer-led practices, such as community-developed consent frameworks, the use of intimacy coordinators, and individual performer contracts, are integrated into platform-level systems. Special attention will be given to the specific challenges presented by live camming, an unscripted and spontaneous content format, and the safeguards in place to prevent trafficking in human beings for sexual exploitation.

The project will rely on a comprehensive, methodologically sound approach that goes beyond anecdotal evidence by collecting data through interviews and surveys across all EU Member States. It will specifically incorporate the perspectives of marginalized and vulnerable groups, including members of the LGBTQ+ community, migrants, racialized individuals, and persons from the Global South or conflict regions. The findings, delivered in the form of regular reports, datasets, and targeted analyses, will equip the European Commission with the information needed to effectively monitor compliance and enforce the DSA against the three designated platforms.

Maximum value of the procurement: 142.000 EUR - Contract duration 12 months

title: Support contract on financial scams Study
description:
Online financial scams are deceptive practices carried out through online platforms that aim to mislead users into disclosing financial data or transferring funds, often in breach of platforms’ terms and conditions and user safety obligations under the DSA. These include investment fraud, impersonation, romance scams (such as sextortion), and marketplace deception involving fake or undelivered products. Online financial scams fall within the systemic risk categories set out in Articles 34 and 35 of the DSA, notably in relation to the dissemination of illegal content and risks to fundamental rights, including consumer protection. These issues intersect with additional obligations under the DSA, such as advertising transparency, protection of minors, and notice-and-action mechanisms for illegal content. Recent developments - such as the designation of the Central Bank of Ireland as a trusted flagger by the Irish Digital Services Coordinator, Coimisiún na Meán - highlight the growing role of financial authorities in the enforcement landscape. Trusted flagger status allows such authorities to issue priority notices to platforms, enabling faster removal of illegal scam content.

Against this regulatory backdrop, the European Commission seeks to expand its knowledge base and analytical capabilities in relation to financial scams occurring on designated platforms. The goal of this study is to support the Commission’s supervisory and enforcement tasks under the DSA by providing a typological mapping of financial scam formats across online platforms and assessing existing and emerging mitigation strategies. The study will not evaluate compliance by VLOPs or VLOSEs but will offer a high-quality analytical overview of the current landscape.

A deeper understanding of financial scams and their evolving formats is essential to the effective implementation of the DSA. The study will generate insights into the scale and scope of fraudulent activities online and help identify best practices for early risk detection and mitigation. Its findings will strengthen the Commission’s capacity for data-driven decision-making and contribute to a more resilient digital ecosystem.

Hence, the goal of this study is to support the Commission’s supervisory and enforcement tasks under the DSA by providing a typological mapping of financial scam formats across online platforms and assessing existing and emerging mitigation strategies. The study will not evaluate compliance by VLOPs or VLOSEs but will offer a high-quality analytical overview of the current landscape.

title: User-friendliness of features employed by OMPs / Features employed by OMPs influencing users behavior
description:
Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 October 2022 on a Single Market for Digital Services and amending Directive 2000/31/EC (Digital Services Act - “DSA”), fully enforceable since 17 February 2024, applies to all online intermediaries in the EU including providers of online platforms that allow consumers to conclude distance contracts with traders (“online marketplaces”), offering their services in the single market, irrespective of whether they are established in the EU or outside. It imposes asymmetric due diligence obligations on different types of intermediaries depending on the nature of their services as well as on their size and impact, to ensure that their services are not misused for illegal activities and that providers operate responsibly. Online platforms are subject to general due diligence obligations under the DSA, including rules to prevent the spread of illegal content (Article 16) and requirements for transparency in advertising systems (Articles 26). In addition to these general obligations, online marketplaces must comply with specific rules outlined in Articles 30 to 32 of the DSA.

The DSA contains also several transparency obligations directed towards consumers. These include advertising transparency (Article 26 DSA), user-friendly notice and action mechanism (Article 16 DSA), and transparent online interfaces for online marketplaces (Article 30 & 31 DSA). The impact of these obligations translates directly into the ability of consumers to find and make use of them. 

Certain substantive obligations are also limited only to Very Large Online Platforms (VLOPs) and Very Large Search Engines (VLOSEs) – i.e. those that reach more than 10% of the EU’s population and have a central role in facilitating the public debate and economic transactions. The DSA also creates for VLOPs and VLOSEs a risk-based approach combined with a stronger public oversight mechanism with the European Commission (“Commission”) being the sole enforcer of the rules.

The above rules share the feature of empowering users to conduct specific actions on the platform or obtain information about either the platform or the platforms offerings. Therefore, it is important to assess the ability of users to benefit from these opportunities in practice, based on how online platforms have currently implemented their obligations under the DSA. 

In the context of the Commission’s effort to verify the compliance of very large online marketplaces with the requirements under the DSA and to gain a more comprehensive, holistic and EU-wide perspective on the implementation of the user-friendliness obligations by a set of very large online marketplaces, the Commission is seeking support from a suitable third-party contractor.

The study will assist the Commission in the execution of its monitoring and enforcement activities as the primary enforcer of the DSA, in line with Art. 72 DSA, more specifically as regards provisions applicable to very large online marketplaces. To this aim, it will support the Commission enforcement activities in assessing the compliance by the designated very large online marketplaces with the obligations that involve enabling the user to access information or perform actions. The specific objectives of the study are to support the work of the Commission by providing: 
• Evidence and data relating to the user friendliness of the features of selected very large online marketplaces with a set of DSA obligations 
• Analysis of user friendliness by the selected very large online marketplaces with a set of DSA obligations
Maximum total contract value: 142,000 EUR.

title: Support Contract on adherence to accessibility requirements by providers of Very Large Online Platforms and Search Engines
description:
Estimated total maximum value (EUR): € 60,000 --- Maximum contract duration: 24 months 
This support contract will support the Commission in effectively encouraging and facilitating a code of conduct for accessibility in line with Article 47 of Regulation 2022/2065 on a Single Market For Digital Services and amending Directive 2000/31/EC (Digital Services Act). 

The primary focus of the support contract is therefore to perform evidence-gathering regarding accessibility issues in the context of Very Large Online Platforms (VLOPs) and Very Large Online Search Engines (VLOSEs) in the sense of Regulation 2022/2065; specifically to identify accessibility concerns within the risk assessment framework of Article 34 and potential risk mitigation measures in line with Article 35.

Article 47 of Regulation 2022/2065 mandates the Commission with encouraging and facilitating the drawing up of codes of conduct at Union level with the involvement of providers of online platforms and other relevant service providers, organisations representing recipients of the service and civil society organisations or relevant authorities to promote full and effective, equal participation, by improving access to online services that, through their initial design or subsequent adaptation, address the particular needs of persons with disabilities. This mandate entails that the Commission should make best efforts to create favourable conditions for meeting the deadlines mentioned in Article 47(3) of Regulation 2022/2065 (to “encourage the development” of codes by 18 February 2025 and “encourage [...] their application” by 18 August 2025).

title: Support contract on transparency requirements for recommender systems under Articles 27 and 38 DSA
description:
Estimated total maximum value (EUR): € 142,000 --- Maximum contract duration: 6 months 
Pursuant to article 27 DSA, providers of online platforms must clearly explain in their terms and conditions the main parameters used in their recommender systems, using plain and intelligible language. Moreover, they must explain options for users to modify or influence these main parameters. The main parameters that must be explained include (a) the most significant criteria used to determine suggested information, and (b) the reasons for the relative importance of these parameters. For platforms offering multiple options for recommender systems, they must provide a functionality allowing users to select and modify their preferred option at any time. Such a functionality should be directly and easily accessible from the section of the platform’s interface where the information is prioritised. In addition to the obligations established by article 27, providers of VLOPs and VLOSEs have an additional requirement: they must provide at least one recommender system option that is not based on profiling as defined in Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (“General Data Protection Regulation” or “GDPR”). Providers of VLOPs and VLOSEs should consistently ensure that users enjoy alternative options which are not based on profiling, for the main parameters of their recommender systems. Such choices should be directly accessible from the online interface where the recommendations are presented. 

This contract will support the Commission in in the execution of its monitoring and enforcement activities as the primary enforcer of the DSA, in line with Art. 72 DSA, more specifically by monitoring and verifying how VLOPs have operationalized the requirements set out in articles 27 and 38. The insights gained from this study will support the Commission’s supervision and enforcement activities in assessing the compliance by the VLOPs and VLOSEs with the obligations that involve informing users about the functioning of recommender systems and offering them more choices. To this end, this study is aimed to gather evidence from users and map out providers of VLOPs’ approaches to the transparency and non-profiling aspects of recommender systems provisions of the DSA, namely articles 27 and 38.

The study aims at providing a comprehensive overview of the operationalization of the transparency requirements of recommender systems across VLOPs and compare them against existing good practices.

In addition to the obligations established by article 27, providers of VLOPs and VLOSEs have an additional requirement: they must provide at least one recommender system option that is not based on profiling as defined in Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (“General Data Protection Regulation” or “GDPR”). Providers of VLOPs and VLOSEs should consistently ensure that users enjoy alternative options which are not based on profiling, for the main parameters of their recommender systems. Such choices should be directly accessible from the online interface where the recommendations are presented. 

This contract will support the Commission in in the execution of its monitoring and enforcement activities as the primary enforcer of the DSA, in line with Art. 72 DSA, more specifically by monitoring and verifying how VLOPs have operationalized the requirements set out in articles 27 and 38. The insights gained from this study will support the Commission’s supervision and enforcement activities in assessing the compliance by the VLOPs and VLOSEs with the obligations that involve informing users about the functioning of recommender systems and offering them more choices. To this end, this study is aimed to gather evidence from users and map out providers of VLOPs’ approaches to the transparency and non-profiling aspects of recommender systems provisions of the DSA, namely articles 27 and 38.

The study aims at providing a comprehensive overview of the operationalization of the transparency requirements of recommender systems across VLOPs and compare them against existing good practices.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ACT: TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE FOR AI SAFETY
description:
Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), which has entered into force on the 1st of August 2024, and for which certain rules will become applicable on the 2nd of August 2025 establishes a comprehensive legal framework governing the area of Artificial Intelligence, and in particular relevance to this procurement, establishes responsibilities for providers of General-Purpose Artificial Intelligence (GPAI) models, aiming to ensure transparency, safety, and accountability in the deployment and use of AI technologies.

Articles 89 and 92 of the AI Act respectively allow the AI Office to monitor the compliance with regards to the AI Act and perform evaluations of GPAI models to assess the compliance and investigate systemic risks at Union level. Article 93 of the AI Act allows the Commission to request providers to take appropriate measures to comply with the obligations, to implement mitigation measures, or to restrict the availability of the model.

In order to carry out these enforcement tasks in relation the AI Act, the AI Office is seeking support of suitable third-party contractors to provide technical assistance aimed at supporting the monitoring of compliance, in particular in its assessment of risks posed by GPAI models at Union level. 

This tender has been split into six lots. Five of those lots dedicated to specific systemic risks, namely (i) CBRN risks, (ii) cyber offence risks, (iii) loss of control risks, (iv) harmful manipulation risks and (v) sociotechnical risks. These lots all share a similar tasks and services:
•	The organisation of multiple risk modelling workshops together with the AI Office, producing a risk model, risk scenarios, as well as corresponding thresholds, informing further work on evaluations. 
•	The development of newly evaluation tools that are private to the Commission.
•	The onboarding of existing evaluations that are publicly available into the developed risk framework. 
•	The creation of a reference procedure and reporting template for doing risk assessment with respect to the developed evaluations.
•	Ad hoc and on demand services for complex evaluations, including for example red-teaming and uplift studies.
•	A risk monitoring service in the form of regular briefings on new developments (e.g. models, risk sources, elicitation techniques, mitigation, incidents) to complement existing AI Office monitoring actions.
The scope of these tasks varies by lot.

Furthermore, there is one lot that is cross-cutting across various risk.
•	Lot 6: agentic evaluation interface, procuring software, Cloud infrastructure support, and methodology to evaluate GPAI on diverse types of benchmarks, focusing on agentic interaction and complex agentic benchmarks.

title: Virtual Human Twins Platform Project Support Office
description: On 16 April 2024, the European Commission launched a call for tenders for a procurement of a state-of-the-art platform for advanced VHT integration and validation models (henceforth referred to as VHT Platform), funded under the Digital Europe Work Programme 2023-2024. The main objective is to develop a distributed platform enabling users to develop, test and integrate VHT models. In the context of the VHT Platform, the Commission is launching this procurement to establish a Project Support office (PSO) that will provide support and advice in managing the Advanced VHT Platform framework contract (FWC) and specific contract(s). The PSO will provide quality assurance for all the deliverables produced by the contractors, and offer strategic and technical advice to assist the Contracting Authority. The ultimate aim of this procurement is for the PSO to assist the Contracting Authority in ensuring that the work of the Advanced VHT Platform contractors adheres to the highest quality standards, methodologies and best practices, meeting all specifications outlined in the Advanced VHT Platform contract. Moreover, the PSO will aid the Contracting Authority in efficiently and effectively managing the Advanced VHT Platform contract and contractors, thus contributing to the successful execution and delivery of the Advanced VHT Platform project and to fulfilling the objectives of the European Virtual Human Twins Initiative.

title: Digital Twin Scenarios: defining a harmonised framework for communicating uncertainty aspects
contractingAuthority: European Commission, DG CNECT - Communications Networks, Content and Technology
ragText:
Procurement: Digital Twin Scenarios: defining a harmonised framework for communicating uncertainty aspects
Call identifier: EC-CNECT/LUX/2025/MVP/0054-EXA
Contracting authority: European Commission, DG CNECT - Communications Networks, Content and Technology
Description: The purpose of this study is to define a framework to address the communication of uncertainty in Destination Earth and to demonstrate the feasibility of the framework, via a functional demonstrator. 
 
Destination Earth (DestinE) is a flagship initiative of the European Commission to develop a highly accurate digital model of the Earth (a digital twin of the Earth) to model, monitor and simulate natural phenomena, hazards and related human activities, including those related to future climate and extreme-weather events. 

This study explores how to effectively communicate uncertainty to policymakers using standardized and reliable methods. It focuses on methods and semantic interoperability frameworks that support decision-making by leveraging predictions and modeling results from digital twins, including those powered by AI-based models. 

It aims to provide guidelines aligned with the Destination Earth Initiative to meet the following objectives:
•	Enhance non-expert users access to reliable, transparent, and traceable data;
•	Establish trustworthy communication practices;
•	Improve communication of uncertainty for decision-makers;
•	Identify and assess interactive tools for uncertainty communication;
•	Strengthen the science and policy interplay.

Maximum total value: 140,000 EUR.

title: Review of Copyright in the DSM Directive
description:
Directive 2019/790 on copyright and related rights in the Digital Single Market aims to modernize the EU's copyright framework, promoting creativity, innovation, and fairness. As required under Article 30(1) of the Directive, the Commission must carry out a review of the Directive and present a report on the main findings to the European Parliament, the Council and the European Economic and Social Committee.

The study aims to provide DG CNECT with methodological and analytical support in gathering information on the application of the Directive in Member States and in assessing its impacts on right holders, service providers and users.

title: Procurement for development of open source cybersecurity attestation programmes in line with the Cyber Resilience Act
description:
Article 25 the Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (the Cyber Resilience Act) empowers the European Commission to adopt delegated acts establishing voluntary security attestation programmes allowing the developers or users of free and open-source software (FOSS) as well as other third parties to attest the conformity of such software with all or certain essential cybersecurity requirements or other obligations laid down in the CRA. 

The objective of these attestation programmes is to support and facilitate the due diligence of manufacturers that integrate FOSS components that are not subject to the essential cybersecurity requirements, as such manufacturers need to ensure the compliance of their product as a whole, including vulnerability handling requirements, as well as to contribute to strengthening the security of FOSS that falls outside the scope of the CRA.
The contractor will be responsible for researching and drafting a comprehensive study that outlines how the attestation programmes could function effectively.

Max Value 80,000 EUR. Duration 9 months.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ACT: TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE FOR AI SAFETY
description:
Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), which has entered into force on the 1st of August 2024, and for which certain rules will become applicable on the 2nd of August 2025 establishes a comprehensive legal framework governing the area of Artificial Intelligence, and in particular relevance to this procurement, establishes responsibilities for providers of General-Purpose Artificial Intelligence (GPAI) models, aiming to ensure transparency, safety, and accountability in the deployment and use of AI technologies.

Articles 89 and 92 of the AI Act respectively allow the AI Office to monitor the compliance with regards to the AI Act and perform evaluations of GPAI models to assess the compliance and investigate systemic risks at Union level. Article 93 of the AI Act allows the Commission to request providers to take appropriate measures to comply with the obligations, to implement mitigation measures, or to restrict the availability of the model.

In order to carry out these enforcement tasks in relation the AI Act, the AI Office is seeking support of suitable third-party contractors to provide technical assistance aimed at supporting the monitoring of compliance, in particular in its assessment of risks posed by GPAI models at Union level. 

This tender has been split into six lots. Five of those lots dedicated to specific systemic risks, namely (i) CBRN risks, (ii) cyber offence risks, (iii) loss of control risks, (iv) harmful manipulation risks and (v) sociotechnical risks. These lots all share a similar tasks and services:
•	The organisation of multiple risk modelling workshops together with the AI Office, producing a risk model, risk scenarios, as well as corresponding thresholds, informing further work on evaluations. 
•	The development of newly evaluation tools that are private to the Commission.
•	The onboarding of existing evaluations that are publicly available into the developed risk framework. 
•	The creation of a reference procedure and reporting template for doing risk assessment with respect to the developed evaluations.
•	Ad hoc and on demand services for complex evaluations, including for example red-teaming and uplift studies.
•	A risk monitoring service in the form of regular briefings on new developments (e.g. models, risk sources, elicitation techniques, mitigation, incidents) to complement existing AI Office monitoring actions.
The scope of these tasks varies by lot.

Furthermore, there is one lot that is cross-cutting across various risk.
•	Lot 6: agentic evaluation interface, procuring software, Cloud infrastructure support, and methodology to evaluate GPAI on diverse types of benchmarks, focusing on agentic interaction and complex agentic benchmarks.

title: Measures to support the implementation of the EU Chips Act Pillar III
description:
To move forward with the implementation of the different tasks under the pillar III of the Chips Act and provide support to the European Semiconductor Board, we need to setup a service contract providing analytical, methodological and administrative support.
The objectives of this procurement are to provide analytical, methodological and administrative support to the Commission, in order to implement the EU Chips Act pillar III. Objectives include developing a methodology to address the requirements regarding the strategic mapping, monitoring and crisis activation, defining in a more operational way the critical sectors and providing support during crisis, providing analytical support (including commercial data) for all policy files relative to the semiconductor value chain.
The results will be used by the Commission and the European Semiconductor Board to fulfil the obligations stemming from the European Chips Act Pillar III.

title: Study to support the evaluation and review of Audiovisual Media Services Directive
description:
Article 33 AVMSD requires that by 19 December 2026 at the latest, the Commission shall submit to the European Parliament and the Council an ex-post evaluation of the impact of the Directive and its added value, accompanied where appropriate by proposals for its review. This study will be the basis for such ex-post evaluation and possible review of the Directive. 
Additionally, Article 13 and Article 16 AVMSD require the Commission to report, based on the information provided by Member States and on an independent study, on the application of the AVMSD provisions concerning the promotion of European works,including independent productions in television programmes and on-demand services.
The study will have five specific objectives: 1.) Provide the Commission with information and data about the application of the Directive, in particular in the aforementioned areas, in light of the developments of the EU audiovisual market, notably its increasing digitalisation; 2.) Provide the Commission with an objective quantitative and qualitative assessment of the Directive’s implementation, looking particularly at the most significant issues; 3.) With regard to Articles 13, 16 and 17, provide the Commission with information and data required for the monitoring of and reporting on the implementation of the AVMSD rules for the promotion of European works, including independent productions; 4.) Identify, where justified by the above assessment, possible regulatory updates / amendments to the Directive that could bring an improvement to its application and/or to the achievement of its objectives; 5.) Identify and impact-assess the policy options proposed to the Commission to implement the above identified regulatory updates / amendments.
The findings of the study will support the Commission's own ex-post evaluation and impact assessment of possible proposals for revision of the Directive and will be used for reporting on European works as required by AVMSD.

title: eGovernment Benchmark 2026
description: In the context of the Digital Decade Policy Programme (DDPP), the eGovernment Benchmark study gathers all relevant indicators for the annual monitoring of online public services associated with key life events accessible to businesses and citizens within all EU member states. This study is integral to the annual assessment of eGovernment advancements, serving as a critical source for tracking the achievement of DDPP’s general objectives related to eGovernment services. More specifically, the eGovernment benchmark study allows to monitor two of the Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) of the DDPP: the online provision of key public services to citizens and the online provision of key public services to businesses, as defined by the Implementing Decision that establishes key performance indicators to measure progress towards digital targets. This study will support the monitoring of the public sector digitalisation by executing the next comprehensive data collection, which shall ensure continuity and comparability with respect of the indicators with the ones published in the 2024 eGovernment Benchmark Report. The data and analysis shall be ready for the publication of the 2026 State of the Digital Decade Report, to be published by mid-2026. Moreover, it will provide a comprehensive assessment of the evolution of eGovernment services across all EU countries.

title: Study to assess the feasibility of a central registry of Text and Data Mining opt-out expressed by rightsholders
description: The main purpose of this study is to assess both the opportunity and feasibility of developing a work-based registry of content identifiers and associated metadata that would support – whether centrally or within a federated network– the effective expression of Text and Data Mining (TDM) opt-outs for copyright-protected works and other subject matter and facilitate their identification by AI developers. The study should explore how a registry could support the expression of the TDM opt-out on individual copyright protected works, on the basis of work-based identifiers and associated metadata supporting right reservation, as well as rights licensing when relevant.

title: Study on EU instruments
description: The overall aim of this study is to support the Commission in its evaluation under Article 91(1) of the Digital Services Act (DSA) and to promote a consistent, clear and effective interpretation and application of the DSA by identifying and analyzing its interaction with other relevant EU legislation. Specifically, the study will provide the Commission with a comprehensive overview of the existing and upcoming EU instruments, the personal and material scope of application of which overlaps or otherwise interacts with that of the DSA. The mapping of the selected legislation will be complemented by an analysis of how these different sets of rules interact with the DSA, with a particular focus on the areas and provisions which might be applied in ways that are not consistent with the DSA and its goals, and on proposals for simplification.

title: Assessing Net Climate Impact of Digital Networks Infrastructures
description:
The task involves examining the feasibility and developing a new methodology to assess the positive carbon impact (handprint) of digital networks infrastructures. The development of a new net carbon impact assessment methodology will be a first of the kind methodology that can estimate the positive impact of digital networks infrastructures in a given geography and context of use.

Existence of such methodology will enable policy makers to deploy digital networks infrastructures that are more sustainable, and, the financial actors to support with sustainable (green, climate) finance the deployment of digital networks infrastructures that, under given conditions, will have a positive impact on climate. 

The task supports the top priority of the Commission, namely the green digital twin transition.

title: Development, Consultancy and Support for an Age Verification Solution
description: This procurement will enable users of online web services to prove their age through the presentation of an electronic attestation through a dedicated application (mobile app) in a privacy preserving manner in order to access age restricted content. This mobile app will directly contribute to the implementation of the provisions on protection of minors of the Digital Services Act (DSA). The application will be built in compliance with the emerging technical specifications of the European Digital Identity Wallet (European Digital Identity · GitHub) and integrated into the common specifications of the European Digital Identity Wallet to be provided by Member States further to Regulation (EU) 1183/2024.

title: Study into how emerging technologies may impact digital market regulation
description: Assessing the foreseeable impact of emerging technologies towards existing online platforms and implementation of the regulatory framework, with particular focus on the DMA. In particular, the study will look into the policies and mitigating measures that the online platforms put in place to deploy emerging technologies taking into account their current and eventual need to comply with the DMA. Monitoring at early stages of the technology life cycle would allow the Commission to proactively and effectively react to any issues and questions concerning effective compliance with the DMA by the gatekeepers.

title: Supporting the evaluation of the Free Flow of Non-Personal Data Regulation, Open Data Directive and Data Governance Act
description:
An evaluation is required for three legislative acts (Free Flow of Non-Personal Data Regulation, Open Data Directive, Data Governance Act) which play an important role in terms of increasing trusted data sharing between sectors and Member States, with a view to creating a single market for data.

The study will assess the benefits of the three acts and shall establish evidence on the achievement of their overall goals. It will provide quantitative and qualitative evidence to the Commission for the preparation of the evaluation reports and potential impact assessments.
