title: Quality of Service performance of roaming services and national 5G networks
description:
Study 2023-005

This study has two overall objectives: 
i.	Quality of service to assess compliance with the Roaming Regulation (EU) 2022/612: To assess the effectiveness of the quality of service obligations in the context of the review of the Roaming Regulation (EU) 2022/612. The study should include some measurements of the quality of service for domestic and roaming data services, including information such as the offered network technology and generations (2G, 3G, 4G, 5G), the typical download and upload speeds, latency, possibly handover quality, e.g. when crossing a country border. The quality of service of the data roaming services shall be compared with the domestic quality of service. In order to ensure the validity of the conclusions, this study will carry out measurements of the data roaming quality in a sufficiently large number of Member States. The study may also explore roaming patterns to better target the measurements. 
ii.	Assessment of the quality of national 5G services: To provide an indication of the overall quality of service for national 5G services in all 27 EU Member States, based on the systematic collection of data regarding national quality of service of 5G networks. The results will feed into the State of the Digital Decade 2025 and 2026 reports. The quality of service measured should include at least the following parameters: download and upload speeds and latency. Additional parameters, if relevant, are welcome. The number of measurements should be sufficient to ensure the statistical validity of the results (national summary). The contractor is free to propose the type of indicators that could best represent the overall quality of 5G service at national level. The results should be comparable between Member States.

title: Purchase of access to and analysis of data on performance of films supported under Films on the Move scheme of Creative Europe: MEDIA Programme and of other types of films.
description:
This call for tender aims to monitor the performance of films recently supported under the MEDIA scheme Films on the Move – their availability, media presence and consumption. 
The requested service consists of two main deliverables:
1) provide online access to the required data in a reader-friendly way (summary by group of titles and/or by individual title), by customizing the database that the service provider owns
2) draft an analytical report based on the quantitative data, including a qualitative analysis on the differences in performance between the titles supported by Films on the Move and non-supported films and releases.
The subject of analysis is Creative Europe: MEDIA call Films on the Move, where distributors benefit from grants to run a larger-than-usual promotion campaign, coordinated across all participating territories to reap benefits of scale, for certain non-national European titles. The purpose of Films on the Move is to increase the audiences to European non-national films thanks to the high quality of the films but also intensive promotion. DG CNECT, which is in charge of the Creative Europe MEDIA Programme, wants to assess the effects of Films on the Move by analysing the data on consumption of the films supported. 
Regarding the (1) customization of the database, the database should include the following categories for analysis: 
-	The data should be provided for 4 categories of films:
o	The titles which received Films on the Move support (around 45 – their choice will be agreed between CNECT and contractor at the start of the contract)
o	The market average for all films released in cinemas in MEDIA countries in the given time frame 
o	The average result of a non-nationally-released film (majority co-) produced in one of countries participating in Creative Europe: MEDIA
o	The average result of a group of selected 10-20 films which are comparable to the titles supported by Films on the Move (similar number of appearances in festivals, nominations and awards). The 10-20 comparable films will be chosen together by the Contractor and DG CNECT at the start of the contract.
-	The performance data on the 4 categories of the films above should be provided preferably broken down for 4 types of geographic regions:
o	The country where it was (majority co-) produced
o	in each country where its distribution is supported by the grant
o	in the rest of the MEDIA-participating countries
o	in the rest of the world (all non-MEDIA participating countries where data is available) – with data also singled out for all available countries, especially US and UK.
-	The data should be provided for the following 3 exploitation windows:
o	Cinemas
	tickets sold in cinemas in general (and in Europa Cinemas in particular)
	number of screenings (and in Europa Cinemas in particular)
	whenever possible, length of regular cinema run (and in Europa Cinemas in particular)
o	TVOD including online services of broadcasters 
	Number of platforms where the title is available, split by local and international platforms
	Whenever possible, length of availability on TVOD platforms, split by local and international platforms
	Wherever possible, number of TVOD purchases, split by local and international platforms
o	SVOD including online services of broadcasters 
	Number of platforms where the title is available, split by local and international platforms
	Whenever possible, Length of availability on SVOD platforms, split by local and international platforms
	Wherever applicable/possible, number of views, split by local and international platforms
-	Additionally, other indicators of performance are welcome. These might be in particular indicators of the film’s popularity and quality assessment (ratings), but other indicators are possible.

title: Venue for the 5th Alliance Forum
description:
We are looking for a venue in Brussels to host an event called “Alliance Forum”. The event is planned for 5 December 2024 (alternative dates: 3 December, 4 December). Number of participants: 100 to 150 persons at the total who will need two rooms in the morning and one room in the afternoon, see distribution below.

The “Alliance Forum” is the umbrella under which we organise two events on the same day: the General Assembly of the European Alliance for Industrial Data, Edge and Cloud (morning) and the Alliance Forum (afternoon only). We expect around 100 to 150 participants at the total. In the morning, for the General Assembly, we will need two rooms, one for 60 persons and one for 90 persons. In the afternoon there should be one plenary room of around 100 to 150 persons. ragText:
Procurement: Development of a study to measure and foster energy efficient and low emission artificial intelligence in the EU
Call identifier: EC-CNECT/2024/OP/0066
Contracting authority: European Commission, DG CNECT - Communications Networks, Content and Technology
Description: Procurement description
-	explore the current and expected carbon footprint of AI;
-	develop a measurement framework which could serve as a basis to address the energy related objectives of the AI Act and also to develop a potential AI energy and emission label;
-	identify the suitable governance and implementation for the measurement framework and; 
-	identify promote energy-efficient and low emission AI best practices through an online repository.

Justification:
AI has a strong potential to solve environmental problems. However, despite its high potential to the environmental and climate crisis, training and executing algorithms imply high- energy consumption and carbon emissions. This environmental impact will increase overtime as the volume of data transferred and stored and the development of AI applications will continue to grow exponentially in the years to come. This study supports the understanding of the issues involved in measuring the environmental impact of the use of AI while identifying possible approaches to incentivising the use of green AI by developers mitigating it.

title: European 5G Observatory "Path to the Digital Decade"
description:
The European 5G Observatory "Path to the Digital Decade" ('the Observatory’) will be the continuation and an extension of the current European 5G Observatory Phase III. The European 5G Observatory initiative was launched in 2018 as a platform to report on 5G network deployment progress and to act as a factual source of information on the development of the EU and global markets of 5G-related products and services. In this context, it has been a main source of information for the monitoring of the implementation of Europe’s 5G Action Plan and for EU policy support in the area of mobile broadband connectivity, leading more recently to the EU connectivity targets 2030. 
Under the new contract, the Observatory will continue to support the Commission services in their policy work in the following key areas: monitoring and assessing the progress of 5G network deployment as well as the EU trajectories and national roadmaps in relation to the implementation of the 2030 Policy Programme “Path to the Digital Decade”, constituting an on-line searchable repository of 5G and 6G related market developments, of spectrum awards and spectrum uses, as well as of new policy initiatives in Member States and worldwide affecting the development of 5G/6G, collecting ad-hoc data on investments in infrastructures, and assisting the Commission services in their collaboration with Member States on 5G policies (KPIs, etc). 
The information and advice and opinions produced by the Observatory will contribute to the overall debate on achieving the EU objectives in the area of mobile broadband connectivity, including supporting the definition of appropriate KPIs in this respect, and the collection of data from Member States. The new Observatory should also strengthen its capacity to track developments in key economic areas outside the Union and enlarge its scope to include advanced 5G, other equivalent connectivity technologies and relevant infrastructures (like edge clouds or NaaS), as well as the early aspects regarding 6G.

title: Digital Services Act - Study on systemic risks and their mitigation
description:
The main purpose of the study is to obtain support for the Commission in its supervisory tasks under the DSA, including its effective enforcement, and to provide relevant insights to support the Commission in preparing a report required under Article 35(2) of the DSA. 
With this study, the Commission is seeking support of suitable third-party contractors to support the analysis of compliance with Articles 34 and 35 DSA as well as to further the Commission’s understanding of systemic risks, their identification, analysis, and assessment, as well as proposed and implemented approaches to their mitigation, and of potential benchmarks and best practices, based on an objective, evidence-based, scientifically sound approach. 
This study should inform with scientific and technical and other relevant insights the Commission’s work on the first edition of a report on systemic risks and their mitigation, as referred to in Article 35(2) DSA.

title: Platform for Advanced Virtual Human Twin (VHT) Models
description:
A virtual human twin (VHT) is a computational model of human patho-physiological processes at different anatomical scales. VHTs hold enormous potential in health and care, namely by delivering on personalised care from targeted prevention to tailored clinical pathways and supporting healthcare professionals in virtual environments (e.g. from medical training to surgical intervention planning) and the virtual worlds. They can make a significant contribution to achieving the goals of the European Health Union. 

The main objective of this action is to develop a distributed platform making available to users (1) a federated repository of VHTs related resources, (2) a combined set of open source software toolkits, and (3) access to computational services, enabling them to develop, test and integrate VHT models. The software toolkits to access the platform repository and services will be deployed and hosted by each user organisation or institution. 

The platform will be used by researchers, developers, engineers, practitioners, innovators in the health and care domain, including for professional training and educational purposes. It will provide controlled and secure access to an environment of simulation and visualisation tools. It will also include openly accessible and proprietary data and model assets for advanced modelling. The platform will be used for developing, testing and integrating existing and new VHT models, based on reference datasets, other research outputs and user resources, and will be fully interoperable with augmented and virtual reality environments. Its use will be based on access to computational services enabled by strategic digital capabilities (e.g. HPC, cloud, edge computing, AI), with links to suitable testing and experimentation facilities (e.g. the healthcare TEF for AI) and other resources becoming available in the context of the European Health Data Space.

title: Platform for Advanced Virtual Human Twin (VHT) Models
description:
A virtual human twin (VHT) is a computational model of human patho-physiological processes at different anatomical scales. VHTs hold enormous potential in health and care, namely by delivering on personalised care from targeted prevention to tailored clinical pathways and supporting healthcare professionals in virtual environments (e.g. from medical training to surgical intervention planning) and the virtual worlds. They can make a significant contribution to achieving the goals of the European Health Union. 

The main objective of this action is to develop a distributed platform making available to users (1) a federated repository of VHTs related resources, (2) a combined set of open source software toolkits, and (3) access to computational services, enabling them to develop, test and integrate VHT models. The software toolkits to access the platform repository and services will be deployed and hosted by each user organisation or institution. 

The platform will be used by researchers, developers, engineers, practitioners, innovators in the health and care domain, including for professional training and educational purposes. It will provide controlled and secure access to an environment of simulation and visualisation tools. It will also include openly accessible and proprietary data and model assets for advanced modelling. The platform will be used for developing, testing and integrating existing and new VHT models, based on reference datasets, other research outputs and user resources, and will be fully interoperable with augmented and virtual reality environments. Its use will be based on access to computational services enabled by strategic digital capabilities (e.g. HPC, cloud, edge computing, AI), with links to suitable testing and experimentation facilities (e.g. the healthcare TEF for AI) and other resources becoming available in the context of the European Health Data Space.

title: A Space for the Metaverse – Virtual World and the transition to Web 4.0
description:
This pilot project will aim at informing the EU policy makers and stakeholders of the challenges and governance needs arising from the development of cutting-edge Virtual World and Web 4.0 technologies, as well as fostering a discussion on global governance with policy makers, civil society, private companies and the technical community.
In particular, this project will have a strong focus on the promotion of European-led global standards, and the identification with stakeholders of potential global multi-stakeholder governance models that would allow the achievement of an open, interoperable, decentralised and rights-based Virtual World and Web 4.0.
Furthermore, this project will facilitate communication and discussion between academia, policy makers and stakeholders to build a strong and competitive ecosystem toward an open, decentralised, trustworthy European and global Virtual World and Web 4.0 that reflect EU values and fundamental rights.

title: European 5G Observatory, Phase III
description: The importance of dynamic policy-making has increased in the rapidly changing environment of today's global economy. The EU policy makers need accurate and up-to-date market information relevant for their purposes. To take informed decisions leading to appropriate actions in its policy-making process, the Commission needs to continue monitoring industry's progress and the relevant developments in light of the goals of the 5G Action Plan (5GAP). The reporting should provide qualitative and quantitative information on actual and likely market developments as well as relevant preparatory actions by private and public actors in the area of 5G. These developments need to be analysed as regards their strategic implications in the context of the 5GAP and other public policy objectives. Main focus should be on developments in Europe, whereas major international developments with possible direct or indirect impact on the European market should also be analysed.

title: Study on current and good practices for the collection, maintenance and accessibility of domain name registration data (“WHOIS data”)
contractingAuthority: null
ragText:
Procurement: Study on current and good practices for the collection, maintenance and accessibility of domain name registration data (“WHOIS data”)
Call identifier: CNECT/2022/MVP/0131-ExA
Contracting authority: null
Description: Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 
The purpose of the present Call for Tender is to conduct a Study on domain name registration data (so-called “WHOIS data”), covering the most important steps in their “lifecycle” from the data collection to the disclosure.The importance of the DNS is recognised in the Directive on Security of Networks and Information Systems (“NIS1 Directive”) as well as in the revised NIS2 Directive. The same NIS2 Directive recognises the importance of maintaining accurate and complete databases of domain names registration data and providing lawful access to such data to ensure the security, stability and resilience of the DNS, which in turn contributes to a high common level of cybersecurity across the Union. 
The objective of this call for tender is to achieve a comprehensive picture of the landscape of current and forthcoming industry practices and technologies of registration that could support the implementation phase of the NIS2 Directive. Today, there is a variety of European and international practices concerning all phases of the establishment and maintenance of domain name registration databases (collection, maintenance, publication and disclosure of data) by TLD registries and registrars, and potentially practices in other digital industries can provide good models for DNS operators. The Study should gather in-depth knowledge of such practices. In particular, the Study should identify and analyse:
-the most prevalent practices for the collection and maintenance of accurate and complete domain name registration data;
-the practices for the verification of domain name registration data, including the use of innovative Know Your Customer (KYC) technologies, electronic Identity (eID), machine-learning technologies;
-the practices for the publication and disclosure of domain name registration data;
-emerging good practices for the collection, verification and disclosure of DNS data in terms of ensuring the maintenance of accurate and complete databases and practices that proved to be effective for the publication of domain name registration data and the timely disclosure of the data to legitimate access seekers. The Study should also explore whether there are practices that have proven to be effective against DNS abuse;
-advanced practices on the collection and verification of online domain name registration data from other digital industries that could be relevant for the DNS industry.

title: Study on Technical Solutions to Ensure Compatibility, Interoperability, Quality, Reliability and Continuity of Emergency Communications in the Union
description: Directive 2018/1972 obliges the EC to adopt delegated acts to ensure effective access to emergency services through the single European emergency number ‘112’. The study will provide information on existing and potential future technical solutions and standards concerning caller location information (modes of transmission, routing), equivalent access for end-users with disabilities (equivalence requirements, various means of access) and routing to the most appropriate Public Safety Answering Point (for various means of access, and including in roaming). The study will identify the technical and economic feasibility of EU-wide interoperable solutions to ensure emergency communication to all, including when travelling within the EU. It will feed into a conceptual basis for the delegated act(s) by assessing the role for EU-level coordination, solutions and infrastructure, as well as regulatory gaps and need for regulatory intervention for the effective implementation of the solutions.

description: The study has the following specific objectives:1) to provide an objective qualitative and quantitative assessment of the implementation of the Union’s current 2 GHz MSS framework, to give an overview of the 2 GHz MSS spectrum usage and services offered. The analysis should pay special attention to any divergences that may have arisen in implementation at national level;2) to outline current state of play as well as developments and trends in the broader satellite connectivity market globally (e.g. new entrants, services, orbits, mergers), the competitive landscape, the drivers at EU level and globally and the role of the EU players;3) to outline possible usage scenarios for the 2 GHz spectrum after 2027, in line with relevant EU policies and programmes, including the Digital Decade targets and upcoming Secure Connectivity programme.

title: Study on Radio Spectrum Policy Programme: taking stock and discussing future scenarios
description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 
In the context of spectrum management for the Digital Decade, the new (second) Radio Spectrum Policy Programme (RSPP) has been included in the Commission work programme for 2023, as a legislative initiative with an impact assessment. The Commission proposal for an RSPP is planned for adoption in the third quarter of 2023. The impact assessment will be supported by a study, which is the subject of this call for tenders. 
 

The strategic priorities of the EU-level spectrum policy are set in the currently applicable (first) RSPP, adopted in 2012. That RSPP forms part of a larger EU regulatory framework for spectrum, along with the 2002 Radio Spectrum Decision, that sets the principles for spectrum policy coordination and harmonized spectrum use in the EU, the 2018 European Electronic Communications Code, that includes provisions on coherent radio spectrum authorisation and integrates radio spectrum policy in the new European electronic communications framework.
The study will aim at taking stock of the application of the 2012 RSPP to date and further focus on assessing the future trends of radio spectrum policy. The contractor will be required to help identifying and describing the problems to be tackled, refining the objectives for EU action, formulating policy options and assessing their potential impacts, costs and benefits, as well as identifying a preferred option, and setting out how the expected results will be monitored and evaluated.
 

It is paramount to reflect new or emerging EU policy priorities including reinforcing EU safety and digital and political sovereignty in the policy principles and actions of the RSPP. A new RSPP will provide strategic planning for spectrum management at least up to 2030, by fostering spectrum governance, reinforcing the common market perspective, and ensuring effective and efficient spectrum management in support of the EU policy objectives (e.g. those set out in the European Green Deal, the New Industrial Strategy for Europe, the new Space Policy). It must contribute to the achievement of the ambitious Digital Decade targets, and focus on strategic policy needs (e.g., 6G, green deal, quantum, space, automated transport, IoT, WiFi, metaverse).
 

The study should also address the fragmentation of the EU-level spectrum market, which leads to (co-ordination) costs, undermines the incentives to invest in networks and impairs the provision of advanced connectivity devices and services. The diversity of authorisation practices (such as auction design) across the EU, especially in terms of setting prices, spectrum caps and timing, may adversely shape markets and hinder investment. There is a need, therefore, to reinforce a common market perspective of radio spectrum.
 

The study should explore how the digital transformation and in particular the evolving wireless communication needs are driving the growing demand for efficient and coherent spectrum management. The deployment of new technologies and mechanisms, such as Artificial Intelligence and automation techniques, can boost efficient spectrum use, e.g. through sharing and flexible licensing. Furthermore, the pan-European nature of services enabled by wireless communications, such as connected cars/trains or remote healthcare, calls for a coherent cross-border approach.

Total maximum value: € 100,000. Maximum contract duration: 5 months.

title: Study on the System Architecture of a Quantum Communication Infrastructure — CNECT/LUX/2020/CPN/0062
description: The objective is to conduct a system study to define the architecture and design the system of a Quantum Communication Infrastructure (QCI) for both the Terrestrial and Space segments. The tender will provide a roadmap for the deployment of the architecture with the key technologies and technology components required for the terrestrial and space segment, including R&D efforts. The costs and timelines associated to the different phases of the deployment will be explained and detailed. The architecture will have to be modular and scalable to include any new application or technology when available. This tender is part of a coordinated call with the European Space Agency (ESA) which will launch the same study but for the space segment of the architecture. The present call addresses only the terrestrial segment.

title: Study supporting the drafting of model contractual clauses under the Data Governance Act on the reuse outside the EU of protected data held by the public sector
description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 

Chapter II of the Data Governance Act regulates the reuse of protected, publicly held data. Under Article 5(11), the Commission is mandated to develop model contractual clauses that public sector bodies may use when allowing the reuse of such data outside the EU. This includes data that originally contained commercially sensitive information, such as trade secrets or IP, but that have been modified for the purposes of the reuse or that were permitted to be accessed in a secure processing environment controlled by a public sector body. The Commission may propose a set of such model contractual clauses by way of an implementing act. This study will support the development of those model contractual clauses. 
By bringing their technical and legal expertise on the reuse of non-personal, protected data held in public registers, the contractor will compile a comprehensive set of clauses currently used and will assess their impact on the reuse of such data outside the EU. The contractor will also identify and analyse the risks resulting from the reuse. Based on the above, the contractor will draft a set of contractual clauses that public sector bodies may rely on when granting access to data for reuse outside the EU. --- Estimated total maximum value (EUR): € 40,000 --- Maximum contract duration: 4 months

description: The objective of this pilot project is to build strong links between Innovation Radar innovators, European investors, and policy makers, with a view to increasing activity and interactions between these communities. The overall goal is to stimulate greater market and societal uptake of ground-breaking innovations emerging from EU-funded research and innovation programmes (such as Horizon Europe, Digital Europe Programme and LIFE). The pilot project should also, by virtue of such interactions and awareness raising, aim to mobilise more European growth capital (including the raising of new funds) that explicitly target EU-funded innovators.

title: Regulatory Sandbox for Blockchain and Legal Advice for EBSI Production Phase - CNECT/2021/OP/0019
description: The objective of the procurement is to contract a consortium that can cover two main responsibilities:1. facilitate and operate (from a legal and administrative perspective) a regulatory sandbox with national and EU regulators for Distributed Ledger Technologies (DLT) in cooperation with the European Blockchain Partnership (EBP). The sandbox will provide legal certainty for, among others, use cases on the European Blockchain Services Infrastructure (EBSI);2. provide to the Commission comprehensive legal advice on all legal and regulatory aspects of operating the EBSI and its use cases, with a minimum of 400 billable hours of legal advice per year (in total 1 200 billable hours). This includes the drafting of legal documents and legal analysis relevant to the transfer of the EBSI onto a special purpose vehicle. Further, the expert will provide advice and legal drafting on/for data protection and intellectual property rights.

title: Study on pornographic platforms
description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 

With the introduction of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065, commonly known as the Digital Services Act (“DSA”), the European Union has established pioneering regulations aimed at safeguarding the digital landscape in Europe. In December 2023, the European Commission officially designated three online pornographic platforms, namely Pornhub.com, Stripchat.com, and Xvideos.com (the “Three Designated Entities”), as Very Large Online Platforms (“VLOPs”). The designation of the Three Designated Entities requires the Commission to implement and enforce the DSA on this distinctive subset of online platforms, which possess unique characteristics compared to other designated VLOPs. 

The effective enforcement of the DSA by the Commission in relation to the designated VLOPs requires the assistance of third-party contractors to support the monitoring and supervisory work, contributing to an objective and scientific approach. The contractor should gather updated insights specifically tailored to navigate the complex ecosystem of pornographic platforms, ensuring a nuanced and effective approach in enforcing the DSA within this specific context.

Specifically, the contractual objective is to monitor the compliance of the Three Designated Entities with Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 by providing high quality data and evidence. This assistance aids the Commission in its enforcement activities, focusing particularly on four key areas of DSA compliance: 1. Content Moderation; 2. Risk Assessment; 3. Illegal Content and Practices; 4. Protection of Minors.

The contractor will be required to engage in three main research activities that will contribute to the monitoring and enforcement of the DSA obligations: 1. EU/MS Legal Framework Overview; 2. Pornographic Industry Overview with specific reference to the Three Designated Entities; 3. Creation of an Evidence Pipeline for the Analysis of Systemic Risks and Mitigation Measures to Support the Compliance Monitoring and Enforcement of the DSA. The results of these research activities will take the form of regular reports, datasets and ad hoc analyses that will support the Commission’s enforcement tasks.

The awarded contractor shall develop a clear, innovative and multifaceted methodology that encompasses the Three Designated Entities and the areas of study identified, allowing for cross-subject and cross-platform comparisons. This methodology should demonstrate an in-depth understanding of current trends, emerging technologies, and best practices in the field of porn studies, with a specific focus on digital pornography and related illegal content and practices.

Max value 142.999EUR – Duration 5 months

title: Survey of Businesses on the Use of Digital Technologies — CNECT/2020/OP/0004
description: New technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, big data, internet of things (IoT), high performance computing, quantum, cloud computing, blockchain, 3D printing are gaining relevance in everyday life of businesses and individuals. The use of digital technologies raises questions how ICT can contribute to the sustainability and a greener economy.Currently, no detailed data are available at member state level on the take-up and other aspects of these technologies. Some reports and statistics already exist, which can provide a basis to develop a European data collection framework.The main objective is to obtain a reliable quantitative overview at member state level on the status of a selection of the above mentioned new technologies and/or to measure how ICT can contribute to sustainability (this study is not about the sustainability of the ICT sector). The list of technologies can vary from year to year (as this study is renewable two times after the first year).

title: EGovernment Benchmark 2023 (Data Collection for 2022, Study Report and Workshop for 2023) – CNECT/2022/OP/0006
description: The eGovernment benchmark exercise aims to obtain a quantitative overview of the status of modernisation of the public sector in a set of relevant countries and disseminate such overview to interested stakeholders and to the public in general. In line with the action plan 2016-2020 and towards supporting the new action plan that will be developed soon, the eGovernment Benchmark aims to assess the provision and implementation of several eGovernment principles (e.g. digital by default, once only principle, inclusiveness and accessibility, openness and transparency, usability, cross-border by default, interoperability by default, trustworthiness and security).The study will support monitoring innovation in the public sector, namely by:(i) executing the collection of data for 2022 eGovernment benchmark; and(ii) analysing the state of play of eGovernment provision across EU countries through the eGovernment benchmark reports and factsheets per country.

title: CNECT/2020/OP/0009 — Study on Copyright and New technologies: Copyright Data Management and Artificial Intelligence — Smart 2019/0038
description: In order to help the European creative industries unleash the potential of new technologies and make the most of them, the Commission would like to look into several specific issues related to: (i) the management of copyright data linked to protected content. The contractor should identify and quantify the economic impact of current issues related to metadata management in the copyright industries. The study should investigate the ways in which new technologies can contribute to improving the efficiency and transparency of licensing of content and management of rights, while making more content accessible for end-users; and (ii) the policy questions related to the interaction between AI and the creative industries, in particular concerning:(a) the use of copyright-protected content as input of AI technologies; and(b) the production of cultural outputs by or with the assistance of AI technologies. The study should provide the empirical basis to carry out a solid analysis from both angles, looking in particular at potential impacts on the European creative industries.The upcoming commission will need to reflect whether policy actions should be considered regarding these areas.

title: Quality of Service performance of roaming services and national 5G networks
description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 
“This study has two overall objectives: (i) Quality of service to assess compliance with the Roaming Regulation (EU) 2022/612: To assess the effectiveness of the quality of service obligations in the context of the review of the Roaming Regulation (EU) 2022/612. In order for the Commission to achieve the roaming review as mandated in the Roaming Regulation (EU) 2022/612 and to meet that specific legal requirement, the study will contribute to the assessment of the quality of roaming services. The study should include some measurements of the quality of service for domestic and roaming data services, including information such as the offered network technology and generations (2G, 3G, 4G, 5G), the typical download and upload speeds, latency, possibly handover quality, e.g. when crossing a country border. The quality of service of the data roaming services shall be compared with the domestic quality of service. In order to ensure the validity of the conclusions, this study will carry out measurements of the data roaming quality in a sufficiently large number of Member States. The study may also explore roaming patterns to better target the measurements. (ii) Assessment of the quality of national 5G services: To provide an indication of the overall quality of service for national 5G services in all 27 EU Member States, based on the systematic collection of data regarding national quality of service of 5G networks. The results will feed into the State of the Digital Decade 2025 and 2026 reports. The Digital Decade Policy Programme sets out a target for 5G connectivity for 2030: “all populated areas should be covered by a next-generation wireless high-speed network with performance at least equivalent to that of 5G”. The current 5G indicator included in the State of the Digital Decade Report measures the availability of the 5G service, not the quality of services. This study should complement the 5G indicator in this respect on a Member State level, by providing data on the quality of 5G services. The quality of service measured should include at least the following parameters: download and upload speeds and latency. Additional parameters, if relevant, are welcome. The number of measurements should be sufficient to ensure the statistical validity of the results (national summary). The contractor is free to propose the type of indicators that could best represent the overall quality of 5G service at national level. The results should be comparable between Member States.)”

description: The project will build on the results of eArk4All and eArk3 grant projects as well as on the eArk specifications. The main tasks of the project will include project management, specifications maintenance and development, validation and conformance testing, outreach and training. The project will also provide support to the generic services projects on eArchiving and ensure the maintenance of the tools used by the entities that have already been onboarded like OP or DG TAXUD.The overarching aim is deployment: reach wider to further domains and extend the take-up of eArchiving services by both public and private entities. All the activities should be carried out with a view to achieve standardisation and integration of selected cross border interoperable digital services.Moreover, the solutions should be compliant with all Member States and EC legislation and recommendations.

title: International benchmarking of the digital transformation
description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 
This study shall compare the EU's digital performance with at least five other countries: the USA (a subset of relevant States may be considered), South Korea, Japan, the United Kingdom and China. Two additional countries must be proposed by the successful tenderer and the final scope of countries must be agreed with the Commission at the inception meeting. 
 
The study shall follow the four cardinal points of the Digital Decade Policy Programme (DDPP). The Commission is currently finalizing the definition of the KPIs to measure the targets of the DDPP and will inform at the inception meeting the successful tenderer about the state of play of the KPIs. The study must align as much as possible to the DDPP KPIs or find alternative indicators that are as close as possible to the DDPP KPIs.
 
In particular, the study shall provide a quantitative analysis comparing the EU with each of the study countries for all the targets, where relevant and comparable data exist. Where possible, the study shall also include in the analysis as many DESI indicators as possible. 

The study shall also develop a qualitative analysis for each study country, describing any relevant national strategies, targets, policy initiatives and funding programmes related to digitalization. 
In particular this analysis should identify the key strengths and weaknesses of these countries with respect to the Digital Decade targets and learn about best practices (successful policies, strategies, actions), where applicable. A comprehensive analysis should be carried out that allows for fact-based comparisons with the EU. Key drivers of successful strategies and most important policy developments should be identified. 
 
Max value: 60,000 EUR, Max contract duration: 3 months

title: Framework Contract for Fixed Price and Quoted Time and Means for Development, Consultancy and Support for the European Digital Identity Wallet
description: The purpose of this tender is to put in place a framework contract for the supply either in fixed price or in quoted time and means to develop and implement the European Digital Identity Wallet based on the proposal for a european digital identity framework and on the accompanying Commission recommendation for a common union toolbox.The wallet and other relevant components will be offered to Member States and other stakeholders for implementing the requirements of the Regulation on a framework for a European Digital Identity. As of end 2022 it will be tested in large-scale pilots.The contract will cover developmental work for a sample wallet, ancillary software for its ecosystem as well as implementation support to Member States between Q4/2022 and 2023.The contractor is expected to develop a prototype wallet (release 1), update this prototype in two subsequent releases. The precise scope and timing of the work will be set out in the specific contracts.

title: Pilot Project — Digital European Platform of Quality Content Providers (2nd Phase)
description: This call for tenders is for the production of a feasibility study identifying the challenges and opportunities in the creation of data space(s) with the aim of fostering data and digital transition across the European news (and content) sectors.The most important aims are:(a) to explore what the data topologies are (e.g. media products, audience data and other relevant data and meta-data) which should be hosted by the data spaces to provide a valuable support to the competitiveness of the news and media content sector;(b) to define the technical requirements needed to build an agile data infrastructure and identify the necessary legal and business frameworks making the data space(s) usable for organisations working across member states borders;(c) to encourage the growth of a coalition of organisations willing to contribute to the development of a European data infrastructure;(d) to collaborate with the first phase of the pilot project for complementary solutions; etc.

It should also link the efforts and outcomes of CEF projects on cybersecurity certification and other relevant projects supported by the CEF or other EU programmes.

title: G02 - Deployment of a Common European Data Space for Cultural Heritage
description: This tender will deploy the common European data space for cultural heritage, to support the digital transformation of Europe’s cultural sector. It will foster the creation and reuse of content in various sectors, with value for the economy and society.The data space will link to relevant European, national and regional initiatives and platforms to provide interoperable access to cultural heritage data in Europe. It will build on the current Europeana DSI and the Europeana Strategy 2020-2025.The objectives are:— to facilitate capacity building in the cultural heritage sector;— to make high-value datasets, in particular 3D, available for scientific research, preservation, restoration, re-use in innovative applications;— to enable easy access to cultural content, allowing stakeholders to use and benefit from this data space;— to create digital opportunities for the public, from virtual visits to history reconstruction and education.

title: Semiconductors market data by feature size, sector and region
description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 
The Service Provider is requested to define and present a methodology for the data collection of market share, by region, for a number of segments in the semiconductor value chain and compile a regional comparison in both relative and absolute terms, in order to track and analyse European progress in meeting the Digital Decade target. 
Task I – Define and formulate a methodology:
Tenderers are asked to propose the specific methodology that covers all aspects of the study, taking into account the context and the objectives of tracking and analysing European progress in meeting the Digital Decade target.
The resultant methodology should be repeatable, clear and well-documented such that third parties or the Commission may potentially adopt the same methodology after the end of this contract. It should be able to produce market share data by segment and overall. 
The methodology should include a detailed explanation about how Europe’s overall market share in the semiconductor value chain is derived from each segment’s market share and list the data sources utilised. The methodology may also propose alternative ways of calculating such overall market share under different assumptions/formulae. 
Unless otherwise agreed on with the Commission, at least the following segments of the semiconductor value chain should be analysed:
•	EDA
•	IP design
•	Manufacturing
o	Microcontrollers and processors
o	DAO
o	Memory
o	Other
•	Materials
o	Raw materials
o	Other
•	Wafer fabrication
•	Equipment
•	Assembly, packaging, and test

for at least the following regions: 
•	United States 
•	Taiwan
•	European Union 
•	UK
•	Rest of Europe
•	Japan
•	China
•	Republic of Korea
•	Rest of the World
The study should also include data and analysis on market share by node-size for the relevant segments of the value chain.
For all regions, the analysis of production in different segments should include companies headquartered within the region and foreign subsidiaries jointly. For the EU in particular, an additional analysis should also distinguish between EU headquartered companies and foreign subsidiaries.
Task II – Report on progress towards the Digital Decade target:
The study must thoroughly analyse European progress in market share in light of the Digital Decade target of 20% of world semiconductor production in value. The report must be accompanied by all corresponding data sets.
The report must include clear and verifiable figures on market value in both relative and absolute terms. The report should indicate for all the segments listed in Task I, the share by region and the value of each segment vis-à-vis the entire value chain, this should then be used to evaluate each region’s share of the global market value. 
Task III – Two subsequent iterations of the report:
Two subsequent annual iterations of the report set out in Task II, with the same methodology of Task I and requirements set out in Task II. 
Estimated total max value: 138,999 EUR. Maximum duration: 36 months.

title: Study on the Economic Potential of Far Edge Computing in the Future Smart Internet of Things
description: The aim of the study is to analyse Europe’s economic opportunities and to derive solid economic data, as well as future policy development for Euope’s digital, industrial and green strategies. Our objectives are:1) To identify and measure the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and challenges of European stakeholders and their competitiveness in a cloud continuum with strong growth at the Far Edge;2) To quantify with broad and robust data Europe’s economic opportunities, in general and in four important vertical areas: mobility, agriculture, energy, and manufacturing;3) To derive scenarios in said sectors, which demonstrate ecological and green benefits of strengthening Far Edge computing;4) To discuss the impact of Far Edge computing in the context of the European data, industrial and green strategies;5) To identify and evaluate the potential impact of European measures at programme and policy level in order to support this opportunity for European industry.

title: Preparation of the groundwork for an implementing act on electronic ledgers and their technical specification
description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 

The proposal for a Digital Identity Regulation (EUDI proposal) mandates the European Commission to adopt an implementing act to put forward general rules about electronic ledgers. The EC is issuing a call for tender to recruit experts to conduct preparatory research on requirements to electronic ledgers and to develop their technical specifications (TS). The contractor should conduct a preparatory, comprehensive research to lay the foundations for the standardisation work. The research should compare existing solutions against the essential requirements defined in Art. 45 of the EUDI proposal. The final outcome of this study would be a contribution towards the development of standard(s). 
The final deliverable of this study is a report of around 80-100 pages, which should inter alia serve as a preparatory work focusing on the technical aspects correlated to the implementing act, which could be issued by the EC, in essence recommending standard(s) for the reliability of electronic ledgers. To this end, the contractor should closely cooperate with standardisation bodies which are recognized by the European Standardisation Framework and with relevant stakeholder associations, especially to gather comments on the outcome of this research. Where relevant, the contractor should propose alignments to existing TS to fulfil the requirement of EUDI’s new concept of electronic ledgers.

Tasks:
1: In the first 3 months of the contract, conduct preparatory research to lay the foundations for the standardisation work. The contractor should identify ongoing work at standard stetting bodies and the preliminary overview of technologies and TS for the gap finding exercise.

2: In the first 6 months of the contract, further building on the outcomes of the Task 1 the research will focus on an in-depth analysis of which technologies meet the requirements set in revised Art. 45 (i) of the EUDI proposal, and on an assessment of what it takes to meet those requirements. 

3: Based on Task 1 and Task 2, the contractor should propose solutions to address any identified gaps and prepare a first draft of TS related to electronic ledgers to provide input for the standardisation work.
Max value: 60,000€ - duration: 12 months

title: CNECT/2022/OP/0049 – Participatory Foresight on Next Generation Online Platforms
description: The tender involves the organisation of a foresight exercise into next-generation online platforms and their transformative impacts on the EU's society and economy. The work shall identify emerging trends and develop scenarios for the online platform economy, including from a global perspective. It shall organise dives on specific trends. Technological developments such as virtual/augmented reality, metaverse, sectoral developments in areas such as energy, health and manufacturing as well as concentration of economic power driven by digitisation efficiencies will be investigated. The changing role of the firm and the position of EU SMEs in B2B industrial supply chains should be investigated. This work shall help inform future policy work including for upcoming Commission mandates. It is linked to the Digital Businesses indicator in the Digital Decade. It shall aim to aid EC colleagues’ foresight literacy and help cross-fertilise horizontal platform policy and sectoral policy areas.

title: Testing and Evaluation Infrastructure for EuroQCI – CNECT/2023/OP/0032
description: This procurement covers the prioritisation and the development of test methods and protocols that will allow for the replicable and comparable assessment (i.e., evaluation) of QKD devices and systems’ capabilities and performance. These must cover both security and non-security aspects. The security aspects comprise the establishment of a ‘product security baseline for EuroQCI components’ (this work will have to be carried out in cooperation with relevant national security Authorities, organised by the Commission services) and the development and building of a testing infrastructure necessary and commensurate to evaluate, in accordance with common criteria, security products implementing quantum cryptography. The non-security aspects are expected to cover functional and non-functional properties, including safety.

title: Quality of Service performance of roaming services and national 5G networks
description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 

“This study has two overall objectives: (i) Quality of service to assess compliance with the Roaming Regulation (EU) 2022/612: To assess the effectiveness of the quality of service obligations in the context of the review of the Roaming Regulation (EU) 2022/612. In order for the Commission to achieve the roaming review as mandated in the Roaming Regulation (EU) 2022/612 and to meet that specific legal requirement, the study will contribute to the assessment of the quality of roaming services. The study should include some measurements of the quality of service for domestic and roaming data services, including information such as the offered network technology and generations (2G, 3G, 4G, 5G), the typical download and upload speeds, latency, possibly handover quality, e.g. when crossing a country border. The quality of service of the data roaming services shall be compared with the domestic quality of service. In order to ensure the validity of the conclusions, this study will carry out measurements of the data roaming quality in a sufficiently large number of Member States. The study may also explore roaming patterns to better target the measurements. (ii) Assessment of the quality of national 5G services: To provide an indication of the overall quality of service for national 5G services in all 27 EU Member States, based on the systematic collection of data regarding national quality of service of 5G networks. The results will feed into the State of the Digital Decade 2025 and 2026 reports. The Digital Decade Policy Programme sets out a target for 5G connectivity for 2030: “all populated areas should be covered by a next-generation wireless high-speed network with performance at least equivalent to that of 5G”. The current 5G indicator included in the State of the Digital Decade Report measures the availability of the 5G service, not the quality of services. This study should complement the 5G indicator in this respect on a Member State level, by providing data on the quality of 5G services. The quality of service measured should include at least the following parameters: download and upload speeds and latency. Additional parameters, if relevant, are welcome. The number of measurements should be sufficient to ensure the statistical validity of the results (national summary). The contractor is free to propose the type of indicators that could best represent the overall quality of 5G service at national level. The results should be comparable between Member States.)” Estimated total maximum value (EUR): € 142,999.9 --- Max contract duration:18 months

title: Broadband Coverage in Europe 2022-2024 - CNECT-2021-OP-0081
description: The broadband coverage in Europe study is designed to monitor the progress of EU Member States in the deployment of different broadband networks. This report covers the EU 27, plus Norway and Iceland, and analyses the availability of ten broadband technologies (DSL, VDSL, VDSL2 Vectoring, cable modem DOCSIS 3.0, DOCSIS 3.1, FTTP, FWA, LTE, 5G and satellite) across each market, at national and rural levels. In addition, various combination categories indicating the availability of one or more forms of broadband connection are also published. These cover overall fixed broadband availability, next-generation access (NGA) availability and overall FTTP & DOCSIS 3.1 availability. Europe-wide overview, country comparisons and year-on-year trends are provided in this report, including country chapters.

title: Quality evaluation of free text information in the DSA Transparency Database Article 17 & 24(5) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065
description:
Article 17 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (DSA) obliges providers of hosting services to inform users when they moderate their content and sets out the “clear and specific” information they need to share with users, in particular with regards to explaining how and why their content was moderated, in so-called statements of reasons. Article 24(5) obliges providers of online platforms to submit anonymised versions of such statements of reasons to a publicly accessibly database hosted by the Commission (The DSA Transparency Database), to establish a public track record of the content moderation decisions taken by online platforms for the monitoring of illegal and harmful content online. The data fields which providers of online platforms, including of Very Large Online Platforms (VLOPs) and Very Large Online Search Engines (VLOSEs) need to fill in to complete their submissions are publicly documented (API and Schema - DSA Transparency Database) and have been aligned with the content format required for the DSA’s transparency reports by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2835 as of 1 July 2025. 

To improve the data quality of the submissions to this database and to support the Commission’s DSA compliance monitoring work, the objective of this support contract is to assess the information quality of providers’ submissions to the the free-text data fields of the DSA Transparency Database at scale. The goal of the contract is to develop a methodology for such an assessment and a user friendly tool with which it can be performed in an automated manner, using a machine learning-based approach to support the systematic monitoring of the data quality of the DSA Transparency Database in multiple quality dimensions (including in particular clarity, specificity & relevance). 

The tenderer will develop an information quality assessment framework, including by defining relevant indicators of information quality and completeness (e.g. text complexity, recurring patterns, clarity, reference to the relevant Terms of service section) against which the free text field submissions of the DSA Transparency Database are evaluated and scored. To detect recurring patterns and templated texts used by providers, pattern and part of speech recognition should also be applied. To apply this methodology at scale, the tenderer will train relevant Machine Learning models (including for example a classifier or regressor and a speech model to reconstruct the decision trees of statements of reasons) which can perform such an assessment at scale. To allow for user friendly interactions with the models and to communicate the assessments produced in an understandable and user-friendly manner, the tenderer should develop a graphical user interface which delivers the assessment in the form of user-friendly per-platform visualisations, e.g. in a dashboard interface or through the generation of comparative reports.

Since accurate and granular data from the DSA’s transparency reporting tools, including the DSA Transparency Database, serve as an input into and compliance indicator in many other DSA areas (e.g. systemic risks, protection of minors, online marketplace safety), such a methodology and tool can produce valuable inputs supporting the Commission’s DSA enforcement work also beyond its content moderation transparency provisions.

Duration :6 months 
Maximum Amount 142.000,00 EUR

Description: Article 17 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (DSA) obliges providers of hosting services to inform users when they moderate their content and sets out the “clear and specific” information they need to share with users, in particular with regards to explaining how and why their content was moderated, in so-called statements of reasons. Article 24(5) obliges providers of online platforms to submit anonymised versions of such statements of reasons to a publicly accessibly database hosted by the Commission (The DSA Transparency Database), to establish a public track record of the content moderation decisions taken by online platforms for the monitoring of illegal and harmful content online. The data fields which providers of online platforms, including of Very Large Online Platforms (VLOPs) and Very Large Online Search Engines (VLOSEs) need to fill in to complete their submissions are publicly documented (API and Schema - DSA Transparency Database) and have been aligned with the content format required for the DSA’s transparency reports by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2835 as of 1 July 2025. 

To improve the data quality of the submissions to this database and to support the Commission’s DSA compliance monitoring work, the objective of this support contract is to assess the information quality of providers’ submissions to the the free-text data fields of the DSA Transparency Database at scale. The goal of the contract is to develop a methodology for such an assessment and a user friendly tool with which it can be performed in an automated manner, using a machine learning-based approach to support the systematic monitoring of the data quality of the DSA Transparency Database in multiple quality dimensions (including in particular clarity, specificity & relevance). 

The tenderer will develop an information quality assessment framework, including by defining relevant indicators of information quality and completeness (e.g. text complexity, recurring patterns, clarity, reference to the relevant Terms of service section) against which the free text field submissions of the DSA Transparency Database are evaluated and scored. To detect recurring patterns and templated texts used by providers, pattern and part of speech recognition should also be applied. To apply this methodology at scale, the tenderer will train relevant Machine Learning models (including for example a classifier or regressor and a speech model to reconstruct the decision trees of statements of reasons) which can perform such an assessment at scale. To allow for user friendly interactions with the models and to communicate the assessments produced in an understandable and user-friendly manner, the tenderer should develop a graphical user interface which delivers the assessment in the form of user-friendly per-platform visualisations, e.g. in a dashboard interface or through the generation of comparative reports.

Since accurate and granular data from the DSA’s transparency reporting tools, including the DSA Transparency Database, serve as an input into and compliance indicator in many other DSA areas (e.g. systemic risks, protection of minors, online marketplace safety), such a methodology and tool can produce valuable inputs supporting the Commission’s DSA enforcement work also beyond its content moderation transparency provisions.
